records.summary_en: *The Jersey City News* reported that Dominican soldiers fired upon a landing boat from the American schooner *Henry Crosby* near Azua, critically wounding a sailor and injuring the first officer. The schooner's captain sailed to Azua and filed a formal report with the United States Consul General in Santo Domingo, who forwarded the complaint to Washington. The unprovoked attack was believed to have resulted from soldiers mistaking the crew for insurgents attempting to land and overthrow President Heureaux.
records.summary_es: *The Jersey City News* informó que soldados dominicanos abrieron fuego cerca de Azua contra un bote de desembarco de la goleta estadounidense *Henry Crosby*, hiriendo de gravedad a un marinero y lesionando al primer oficial. El capitán de la goleta navegó hacia Azua y presentó un informe formal ante el cónsul general de los Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo, quien remitió la queja a Washington. Se creía que el ataque no provocado se debió a que los soldados confundieron a la tripulación con insurgentes que intentaban desembarcar para derrocar al presidente Heureaux.
records.passage: drew up in line, and, levelling their carbines at the men in the Crosby's small boat, fired. One of the sailors threw up his hands and fell at the feet of his companions. The others paused in surprise and affright, when suddenly another volley was fired from the shore. By this the first officer was shot. Then the boat was put about and turned towards the schooner. The sailors rowed for their lives. The wounded man was taken aboard the Crosby. Then it was discovered that the first officer had been shot in the shoulder and that the seaman had been struck by several bullets. A wound in the back is believed to be fatal. The Crosby's captain did not know what to make of such barbarous and unwarranted treatment. He hoisted sail and after a time reached the port of Azua. From there he reported the outrage to the United States Consul General at San Domingo City. At the latter's request the full details of the shooting were written out by the captain and the report has been forwarded to the United States authorities at Washington. The letter came by the George W. Clyde and will probably reach the State Department tonight. No information or satisfaction was given to the American skipper by the Dominican authorities. It is supposed, however, that the soldiers believed that the American sailors were a band of conspirators who intended to overthrow the Government of President Heureaux. records.summary_en: The *Weekly Union* reported that a boat crew from the American schooner *Henry Crosby* was fired upon by Dominican troops while approaching the beach near Azua, resulting in severe wounds to the first officer and the fatal shooting of a sailor. The captain reached Azua to lodge an official protest with the United States Consul General, who transmitted the findings to the State Department. Dominican troops reportedly mistook the American boat for an insurgent expedition sent to unseat President Heureaux.
records.summary_es: El *Weekly Union* informó que la tripulación de un bote perteneciente a la goleta estadounidense *Henry Crosby* fue atacada a tiros por tropas dominicanas mientras se aproximaba a la playa cerca de Azua, lo que causó graves heridas al primer oficial y la muerte por disparos de un marinero. El capitán llegó a Azua para presentar una protesta oficial ante el cónsul general de los Estados Unidos, quien transmitió las averiguaciones al Departamento de Estado. Según trascendió, las tropas dominicanas confundieron la embarcación estadounidense con una expedición insurgente enviada para derrocar al presidente Heureaux.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported on an official communication from Dominican President Ulises Heureaux to Vice President Figuereo announcing the summary execution of several political opponents. Heureaux stated that General Eugenio Generoso Marchena and five associates were executed at La Clavellina for the murder of a government delegate, while three others were shot at Los Jovillos for attempting to assassinate Heureaux. Seven other accused conspirators were spared execution and transferred to prison in the capital.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó sobre una comunicación oficial del presidente dominicano Ulises Heureaux al vicepresidente Figuereo en la que anunciaba la ejecución sumaria de varios opositores políticos. Heureaux declaró que el general Eugenio Generoso Marchena y cinco colaboradores fueron fusilados en La Clavellina por el asesinato de un delegado gubernamental, mientras que otros tres fueron pasados por las armas en Los Jovillos por intentar atentar contra la vida de Heureaux. Otros siete acusados de conspiración se salvaron de la ejecución y fueron trasladados a prisión en la capital.

The document says, among other things: "Having carefully sifted the facts and reached the full conviction of the guilt of the accused of the said ambushes and assassinations, acting with justice and with the consciousness of duty, which impose now hard and painful measures, I gave the order to shoot, in the place called 'La Clavellina,' where General Joaquin Campos, Delegate of the General Government, had been assassinated, General Eugenio Generoso Marchena, José Concha, Oliverio Reyes, José Maria Guzman, José Reyes and Carlos Baez Figueroa. And in the place called 'Los Jovillos,' where was the ambush of those who sought to assassinate me on my journey from Neiba to this city (Azua), I have given orders that José Pérez, Pablo Baez and Lorenzo Brito shall be executed. "Although important documents referring to those occurrences incriminate Senors Alfredo Blandino, Abraham Ortiz, Antonio Romano, Manuel [illegible], Prospero [Freites?], Agapito [Felix?] and José Polin [Reyes?], yet, believing that a sufficient example has been made, I have felt bound not to have them executed, and I have put them in the jail of the capital, where they shall remain until otherwise disposed of." records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported on escalating authoritarian measures by President Heureaux, who restricted foreign travel and arrested suspected political opponents across the country. Following Heureaux's armed seizure of $60,000 from a French bank, the bank’s Dominican attorney, Jacinto de Castro Peynado, was imprisoned for his arguments during legal proceedings against the government. Additionally, Dominican troops blocked the son of a former Spanish consul from landing in Santo Domingo, threatening him with rifles until he departed on the steamer.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó sobre la escalada de medidas autoritarias adoptadas por el presidente Heureaux, quien restringió los viajes al extranjero y arrestó a presuntos opositores políticos en todo el país. Tras la incautación armada por parte de Heureaux de 60.000 dólares de un banco francés, el abogado dominicano de la entidad bancaria, Jacinto de Castro Peynado, fue encarcelado a causa de sus alegatos en los procedimientos judiciales contra el gobierno. Además, tropas dominicanas impidieron el desembarco en Santo Domingo del hijo de un excónsul español, amenazándolo con fusiles hasta que abandonó el lugar a bordo del vapor.

records.summary_en: *The Lusk Herald* reported imminent conflict between France and the Dominican Republic after French warships appeared off Santo Domingo City to take soundings. The French government delivered an ultimatum demanding the return of $60,000 seized from a French-backed bank along with a $20,000 indemnity, threatening bombardment if President Heureaux failed to pay. records.full_text:
MAY BOMBARD SAN DOMINGO.

France Demands Indemnity for Confiscation of a French Bank.
New York special: A dispatch to the World, dated Puerto Plat, San Domingo, January 18, says:
“Trouble seems imminent between France and the Dominican Republic. A French man of war appeared off San Domingo City a few days ago and began to take soundings. Soon after she departed another appeared. The latter was boarded by a pilot, who was informed that his services were not needed, and when he asked the commander his intention, he was told it was none of his business.”

The San Domingo authorities had a dispute with a bank a few years ago, and eventually took $60,000 from it. The bank was backed by French capitalists, and the bankers laid the case before the French Government. France demanded that the money be returned to the bank, but diplomatic negotiations seem to have resulted in nothing. The World correspondent learns upon trustworthy authority that the French ultimatum has already been sent in and demands the restoration of the $60,000 and $20,000 as indemnity. President Heuraux, it is said, has declared that he has no money to pay it with.

Dispatches for the Britsh Admiral at Jamaica passed this port probably asking him to look after British interests in case of bombardment.

records.passage: THE PROTOCOL. records.summary_en: The *Evening Bulletin* analyzed legal questions regarding the proposed annexation of Hawaii, citing the Dominican precedent for provisionally maintaining local governance machinery until Congress legislates for a newly incorporated territory. It specifically noted provisions safeguarding congressional authority and prohibiting the entry of Chinese laborers.

In order that this independence of the Congress shall be complete and unquestionable, and pursuant to the recognized doctrine of public law that treaties expire with the independent life of the contracting state, there has been introduced out of abundant caution an express proviso for the determination of all treaties heretofore concluded by Hawaii with foreign nations and the extension to the islands of the treaties of the United States. This leaves Congress free to deal with such especial regulation of the contract labor system of the islands as circumstances may require. There being no general provision of existing statutes to prescribe the form of Government for newly incorporated territory, it was necessary to stipulate, as in the Dominican precedent, for continuing the existing machinery until provision shall be made by law for the Government, as territory of the United States, of the dominion thus incorporated into the union, but having in view the peculiar status created in Hawaii by laws enacted in execution of the treaties heretofore concluded between Hawaii and other countries, only such Hawaiian laws are thus provisionally continued as shall not be incompatible with the Constitution or the laws of the United States or with the provisions of this treaty. Los exiliados dominicanos en Nueva York manifestaron un firme respaldo al movimiento de Moscoso y anticiparon su éxito basándose en informes provenientes de Puerto Plata.

records.full_text:
REVOLUTION FOR SAN DOMINGO.

It Is Being Brewed in New York by Enemies of President Hereaux.

New York, Oct. 21.—The Journal and Advertiser says: Efforts to crystalize the opposition to President Hereaux of San Domingo, the Spanish speaking republican that shares with the French speaking republic of Hayti the West Indian island of Hayti, into a revolution, are said to be nearing completion in this city.

The leader of the movement in New York is given Moscoso, who arrived here last July and is said to have been constantly busy ever since with secret meetings with the purpose in view. He is one of Hereaux's implacable foes and his friends here declare that he is the most available man to lead a revolt against the Dominican ruler. Moscoso was long ago recognized by Hereaux as a dangerous man and Hereaux was scheming to put him in prison and thus get him where he could not endanger the administration, when Moscoso got wind of his intention and promptly skipped out of the country. He went to the neighboring island of Porto Rica, the usual refuge of Dominican exiles, and was nearly assassinated there shortly after. Moscoso's friends openly declare their belief that the would-be assassins were in the pay of President Hereaux, the desperate method having been resorted to, they claim, because Moscoso was rapidly effecting his plans to return secretly to San Domingo and start an uprising, which Hereaux wanted to prevent by any means. Moscoso's assailants in Pence, Porto Rica, came very near killing him. He was taken unawares and stabbed once before he realized his danger, and then managed to escape only because one of the men thinking a fatal blow had been struck ran away, and the other was too scared and bewildered at the flight of his companion to follow up his attack. Moscoso is barely 35 years of age. He was educated in this country and speaks languages with fluency. His personal bravery is extolled as highly as his mental accomplishments, and his following at home is declared to be large and enthusiastic. He refuses to discuss his plans, but talks readily when President Hereaux's administration is mentioned. He makes no secret of his opposition to the president, whom he freely denounces.

Dominican exiles are not numerous in New York but they make up in determination what they lack in numbers. They declare they mean to stake their all in Mocoso's movement and basing their hopes on recent advices chief seaport, are confident that it will be successful.

Hereaux has been president of Santo Domingo three terms, a much longer period than any of his predecessors. His enemies declare that he has been able to retain the reins of president so long because he has been unscrupulous in carrying out his secret intention of making himself dictator for life by stifling opposition by means of bribery and intimidation. In consequence the best and most influential of the country have either been stultified or banished. It is even charged that a number have been unlawfully put to death at the president's instigation.

records.summary_en: *The Saint Paul Globe* published a letter comparing the proposed annexation of Hawaii to President Grant's unsuccessful effort to annex Santo Domingo in 1869 and 1870. The writer recalled that despite strategic arguments, joint resolution efforts, and a favorable commission report, the annexation treaty failed in the Senate. The author argued that past fears of foreign powers absorbing Santo Domingo proved unfounded and hoped Hawaii would avoid annexation.
records.summary_es: *The Saint Paul Globe* publicó una carta en la que comparaba la proyectada anexión de Hawái con la infructuosa tentativa del presidente Grant de anexionar Santo Domingo en 1869 y 1870. El autor recordaba que, a pesar de los argumentos estratégicos, de los esfuerzos por lograr una resolución conjunta y de un informe favorable de la comisión, el tratado de anexión fracasó en el Senado. El autor sostuvo que los temores pasados de que potencias extranjeras absorbieran a Santo Domingo resultaron infundados y expresó su deseo de que Hawái evitara la anexión.
records.passage: HISTORY REPEATS. Similarity in Hawaiian and Santo Dominican Cases. To the Editor of the Globe. About thirty years ago an attempt was made by the Grant administration to annex Santo Domingo, the second largest island in the West Indies, which ingloriously failed, as I hope the present administration will fail in its attempt to annex the Hawaiian islands. Then, as now, a treaty had been signed for annexation between President Grant and the president of the Santo Domingo republic on Sept. 9, 1869, which treaty was rejected by the senate. In December, 1870, inspired by the president's annual message, another attempt was made to annex said island by passing a joint resolution, which then, as it is now claimed, could be accomplished by a majority vote. This was met and it was held that no territory could be annexed without a treaty which must be ratified by a two-thirds vote of the senate. Finally, a commission of visiting statesmen was appointed, who, in due time, reported favorably, but the whole thing was abandoned in the long run, and no "foreign power" has thus far expressed any desire to absorb that republic. The article reviewed the rejection of President Grant's annexation project 28 years prior, which led the Dominican Republic to refuse any sale, cession, or lease of its territory. It emphasized that current American interest did not contemplate territorial annexation or permanent fortifications.

Subrayó que el interés estadounidense en ese momento no contemplaba anexiones territoriales ni fortificaciones permanentes.

Samana Bay not only gives anchorage enough for the fleets of the world, but it is exceedingly well situated for our purpose. It is true that Mole St. Nicolas, on the Windward Passage, between Hayti and Cuba, has strategic advantages, that route being shorter from our ports to the Isthmus, but Samana Bay lies on the Mona Passage, a route which is taken by the merchant vessels that go to South America between San Domingo and Porto Rico. It is healthful, under the trade winds which blow into it, and it is capable of defence, its narrow entrance being commanded by Levantada Island, while the bold headlands on the north shore give a plunging fire. But we are to assume that there is no question whatever of fortifications now, since no annexation of territory is undertaken, nor even any lease from the Dominican Government. It will be remembered that the old project of acquiring Samana Bay as a coaling station, under President Grant's Administration, about twenty-eight years ago, developed into the form of annexing all San Domingo, and this the Senate did not approve. But afterward the little republic took the ground not only that she would not be annexed, but that she would not sell, cede, or even lease us any territory at all. records.summary_en: *The Indianapolis Journal* reported from Haiti regarding proposed constitutional changes concerning foreign property rights. Haitian Foreign Minister Brutus St. Victor denied claims that the government intended to repeal Article 6 of the constitution, which prohibited alien ownership of real estate, stating the public was not prepared for such reform. St. Victor also declined to disclose specific government plans to address the rising premium on paper currency.

El ministro de Asuntos Exteriores haitiano, Brutus St. Victor, desmintió las versiones de que el gobierno pretendiera derogar el artículo 6 de la constitución, que prohibía a los extranjeros la propiedad de bienes inmuebles, afirmando que la opinión pública no estaba preparada para tal cambio. St. Victor declinó asimismo revelar planes gubernamentales específicos para hacer frente al creciente sobreprecio del papel moneda.

A Haitian deputy, who professes to be well informed on all political matters, said yesterday that the government was certain to favor the elimination of Article 6 from the Constitution at the session of the Chambers, which will probably begin this week. The correspondent of the Associated Press derived from Brutus St. Victor, the secretary of state for foreign relations, to-day, an entirely different view of the parliamentary programme. Mr. St. Victor denied categorically that the government contemplated any project for the removal of the prohibition of alien ownership of real property. Such a step, he said, if ever taken, must be yet a very great way off. "The people," he continued, "are not ready to accept a change. There must be a gradual preparation of public sentiment before the government could even suggest it. There is, no doubt, such an opinion favorable to it, but it has as yet manifested only chiefly in the cities, and it must be remembered that the mass of the Haitian population is rural, and that it is strongly wedded to national traditions." records.summary_en: *The News & Observer* reported that an armed uprising against Dominican President Heureaux had begun at Monte Cristi, near the Haitian border. The Clyde Line steamer *Fanita* reportedly departed Cape Haitien carrying 150 Dominican insurgents concealed in its hold, alongside rebel leaders General Juan Isidro Jimenes and General Villanueva. Observers in Haiti described the revolutionary expedition as well prepared and expressed strong confidence in its potential success.

records.summary_en: The *Richmond Dispatch* reported that an attempted revolution against Dominican President Heureaux met swift defeat at Monte Cristi. According to an official dispatch from Heureaux, insurgent leader General Jimenes fled aboard the steamer *Fanita* under fire, while Haitian General Morales and several others were killed. Dominican authorities captured several prisoners, including General Villanueva's son, who were slated for execution.

The report highlighted Jimenes's past role in financing President Hyppolite in Haiti and noted the significant use of a Clyde Line steamer in the conspiracy. records.passage: DOMINICAN UPRISING. Another Report That President Heureaux Has Been Shot. Copyright 1898 by the Associated Press. Cape Haytien, June 7, 7:40 p. m. The Dominican warships Restauracion and Independencia arrived here at 6 o'clock this evening having on board it is understood the prisoners taken in the recent revolutionary attempt headed by Jimenez and Morales. records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported that President Heureaux traveled to Great Inagua to lodge piracy charges against General Juan Isidro Jimenes following the failed Monte Cristi invasion. In an interview aboard his gunboat, Heureaux dismissed Jimenes as a skilled merchant but an inept politician whose revolutionary schemes were childish and thoroughly penetrated by government informants. Heureaux also exhibited seized documents and papers taken from insurgent casualties to demonstrate that the conspiracy was completely neutralized.

records.summary_en: The *Waterbury Evening Democrat* reported that Dominican dissidents were organizing a renewed attempt to overthrow President Heureaux using the sloop *Olivia* to recruit men along Haiti's northern coast for attacks on Monte Cristi or Puerto Plata. Revolutionary agents were also reportedly active in southern Dominican provinces enlisting prominent figures. Additionally, Haitian officials, acting upon the Dominican government's request, ordered the son of rebel leader General Jimenes to leave Haiti.
records.summary_es: El *Waterbury Evening Democrat* informó que disidentes dominicanos organizaban una nueva tentativa para derrocar al presidente Heureaux utilizando la balandra *Olivia* para reclutar hombres en la costa norte de Haití con miras a atacar Monte Cristi o Puerto Plata. Según se informó, agentes revolucionarios actuaban asimismo en las provincias del sur dominicano sumando a destacadas personalidades. Además, funcionarios haitianos, a solicitud del gobierno dominicano, conminaron al hijo del líder rebelde general Jimenes a abandonar el territorio de Haití.

records.summary_en: A report on Dominican politics under President Heureaux describes Emmanuel Jimines as a young man of pleasing manners who has much sympathy, but calls his Monte Cristi attempt one of the worst planned and feeblest ever known. It recounts how Heureaux employs a large number of spies, many of them women, yet is his own best spy, telling of him disguised as a laborer learning of a conspiracy, confronting conspirators in their own meeting, and pardoning a hired assassin who revealed who sent him, while thousands of dollars have secretly been offered for his assassination and the common people believe he leads a charmed life.

records.summary_en: The *Anaconda Standard* published an overview of the Dominican Republic, detailing its geography, population of 610,000, and history from colonial rule through its independence on February 27, 1844. The report described the nation's political structure, public education system, and major agricultural exports, including tobacco, sugar, coffee, and mahogany. It also observed that while rich mineral deposits of gold, copper, and iron existed, the country's mineral resources remained largely undeveloped.
records.summary_es: *The Anaconda Standard* publicó una reseña general de la República Dominicana, detallando su geografía, una población de 610.000 habitantes y su historia desde la época colonial hasta su independencia el 27 de febrero de 1844. El informe describía la estructura política del país, el sistema de educación pública y sus principales exportaciones agrícolas, entre ellas tabaco, azúcar, café y caoba. Observó asimismo que, si bien existían ricos yacimientos minerales de oro, cobre y hierro, los recursos mineros del país permanecían en gran medida inexplotados.
records.passage: expand in the West Indies than in the East Indies. The island of Santo Domingo is the largest of the West Indies next to Cuba. There are two republics on the island, the republic of Dominica being the larger and comprising about two-thirds of the island, while the republic of Hayti occupies the western end of the island. The island was first settled by the Spanish and was called Hispaniola. Then French buccaneers gained a foothold on it. In 1697 the western part was ceded by Spain to France. In 1800 Toussaint Louverture seized the Spanish part of the island and also stirred up an insurrection in the French part. Through treachery he was enticed to France and died in jail. On February 27, 1844, the Spanish or eastern part of the island threw off allegiance to Spain and formed the republic of Dominica. The republic contains 18,045 square miles and has a population of 610,000. The president is elected for four years, chosen by universal suffrage. He is assisted by a congress of twenty-two deputies elected for two years by popular vote with restricted suffrage. The Spanish language is principally spoken. Education is free and obligatory. The schools are good. The products are mainly tobacco, sugar, rice, coffee, maize, cocoa, bananas, pine apples, sweet potatoes and cotton. Gold, silver, copper, coal, iron and tin exist on the island, but no efforts have been made to develop the mineral resources. Logwood and mahogany are among the principal exports. records.headline: This article describes Santo Domingo as long disturbed by dissensions and revolutionary movements, naming Juan
records.summary_en: This article describes Santo Domingo as long disturbed by dissensions and revolutionary movements, naming Juan Jiminez, a former merchant of Monte Christi and permanent candidate for the presidency, as one of the chief troublemakers. It recounts how Jiminez in June 1898 organised a filibustering expedition against the Heureaux government and landed at Monte Christi, but failed, his men being killed or captured while he escaped, and how another invasion was hourly expected there in July; it also describes the country's recent acute financial crisis, when the rate of exchange on New York rose more than 100 per cent and a commercial panic followed.
records.summary_es: Este artículo describe a Santo Domingo como perturbado durante mucho tiempo por disensiones y movimientos revolucionarios, y señala a Juan Jiménez, antiguo comerciante de Monte Cristi y candidato permanente a la presidencia, como uno de los principales agitadores. Cuenta cómo Jiménez organizó en junio de 1898 una expedición filibustera contra el gobierno de Heureaux y desembarcó en Monte Cristi, pero fracasó, pues sus hombres fueron muertos o capturados mientras él escapaba, y cómo en julio se esperaba allí otra invasión de un momento a otro; también describe la reciente crisis financiera aguda del país, cuando el tipo de cambio sobre Nueva York subió más del 100 por ciento y siguió un pánico comercial.
records.passage: iron rule was such bitter hatred on the part of his enemies that they tried to assassinate him in both June and December of 1898. But he escaped, and his opponents feared more than ever his smile which he graciously accorded to each one doomed by him to be shot against the "long, brick wall." Santo Domingo has been disturbed by internal dissensions and revolutionary movements for a long period, one of the chief trouble-makers being Juan Jiminez, formerly a prosperous merchant of Monti Christi, and who considers himself a permanent candidate for the presidency, his father having at one time been president of the republic. Jiminez, in June, 1898, organized a filibustering expedition against the Heureaux government, making a successful landing at Monti Christi. The attempt, however, failed, all Jiminez's men being killed or captured. Jiminez himself escaped, and, on July [illegible] last, it was reported that panic reigned at Monti Christi, where another invasion by Jiminez's followers was hourly expected. The country has also recently passed through an acute financial crisis, owing to the peculiar financial system of the country. records.headline: After the assassination of President Heureaux, Vice President Figueroa, who assumes the presidential functions
records.summary_en: After the assassination of President Heureaux, Vice President Figueroa, who assumes the presidential functions, informed the president's widow that the body would be buried at Santiago de los Caballeros rather than taken to Santo Domingo, for fear of hostile manifestations there. Government officials expect an uprising: arms and ammunition have been ordered sent to Santiago, the assassin's party is reported to be gathering to attack the government troops, and the president was shot down at Moca by Ramon Caceres just as he gave alms to an old man who had asked for help.
records.summary_es: Tras el asesinato del presidente Heureaux, el vicepresidente Figueroa, que asume las funciones presidenciales, informó a la viuda del presidente que el cuerpo sería enterrado en Santiago de los Caballeros en vez de ser llevado a Santo Domingo, por temor a manifestaciones hostiles allí. Las autoridades del gobierno esperan un levantamiento: se ha ordenado enviar armas y municiones a Santiago, se informa que el partido del asesino se está reuniendo para atacar a las tropas del gobierno, y el presidente fue derribado a tiros en Moca por Ramón Cáceres justo cuando daba limosna a un anciano que le había pedido ayuda.
records.passage: public Was Shot Down. FORT DE FRANCE, July 27.—[illegible] financial crisis having arrived in Santo Domingo and an insurrection being feared owing to the number of malcontents, President Heureaux went to the north and west of the island to prepare for all eventualities. He was about to leave Moca for Santiago de los Caballeros when he was killed. Booted and spurred, ready to mount his horse, he sat under the gallery of a house in the Rue Colon, talking to two friends, at 4:30 in the afternoon, when an old man approached to ask for alms. Just as the president gave the old man some money, Caceros, the assassin, rushed forward quickly and fired twice from his revolver. One bullet struck the heart of the president, killing him instantly, and the other killed the old man by his side. The crime was committed so rapidly that the friends of the president were not able to interfere in time to prevent it, but they fired a number of shots at Caceros, who ran away, accompanied by several persons. The assassin's party returned the fire of the president's friends and Caceros escaped. It is not known whether he was wounded or not. The authorities immediately sent troops to pursue him. The body of President Heureaux was taken to the house of the governor of Moca. The news of the president's death spread rapidly and caused much emotion among the inhabitants of the island. An armed band attacked Moca, forces supporting the assassins were reported augmented, and advices from Santo Domingo described a well-planned plot by adherents of Jimenez to depose Heureaux, while General Gomez in Havana refused to discuss the presidency of the Dominican Republic.

Una banda armada atacó Moca, se informó que las fuerzas que apoyaban a los asesinos habían aumentado, y despachos de Santo Domingo describieron un complot bien planeado de partidarios de Jiménez para deponer a Heureaux, mientras el general Gómez en La Habana se negó a hablar de la presidencia de la República Dominicana.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Times-Republican* reported that Washington officials were prepared to intervene and establish a protectorate over the Dominican Republic if violent conflict erupted over the succession to the assassinated President Heureaux. Cuban newspapers debated remarks by General Maximo Gomez's secretary suggesting foreign intervention would be required to maintain order on the island. Meanwhile, Dominican Vice President Wenceslao Figuereo reportedly accepted the presidency to maintain constitutional continuity.

Periódicos cubanos debatieron declaraciones del secretario del general Máximo Gómez en las que sugería que se requeriría una intervención extranjera para preservar el orden en la isla. Entretanto, según se informó, el vicepresidente dominicano Wenceslao Figuereo asumió la presidencia para asegurar la continuidad constitucional.

records.headline: A profile of President Heureaux tells how his brother-in-law, the husband of the half sister for whom he had a real
records.summary_en: A profile of President Heureaux tells how his brother-in-law, the husband of the half sister for whom he had a real affection, was advanced rapidly in the government service, warned once after joining a plot to assassinate the president, and found within six months plotting again. Heureaux gave a state breakfast in the young man's honor, seated him at his side, and as the meal ended told him he was going to be shot in five minutes; the official was then shot in the courtyard while the president's sister screamed from the windows above, and the uncoffined body was quickly buried in a flower garden.
records.summary_es: Un perfil del presidente Heureaux cuenta cómo su cuñado, el esposo de la media hermana por quien sentía un verdadero afecto, fue ascendido rápidamente en el servicio del gobierno, advertido una vez tras unirse a un complot para asesinar al presidente, y descubierto en menos de seis meses conspirando de nuevo. Heureaux ofreció un desayuno de Estado en honor del joven, lo sentó a su lado y, al terminar la comida, le dijo que iba a ser fusilado en cinco minutos; el funcionario fue fusilado entonces en el patio mientras la hermana del presidente gritaba desde las ventanas de arriba, y el cuerpo sin ataúd fue enterrado rápidamente en un jardín de flores.

records.summary_en: A Puerto Plata dispatch dated August 1 calls the situation in Santo Domingo critical after President Heureaux's assassination, with an outbreak expected at any moment and friends of the government under arms to protect property and preserve the peace. It says the assassins, Ramón Cáceres, Manuel Cáceres, Horacio Vásquez and Domingo Pichardo, were in the country about Moca with their followers, that the president was buried with military honors, and that troops were being assembled at Moca and La Vega.

Dice que los asesinos, Ramón Cáceres, Manuel Cáceres, Horacio Vásquez y Domingo Pichardo, estaban en el campo cerca de Moca con sus seguidores, que el presidente fue enterrado con honores militares, y que se estaban reuniendo tropas en Moca y La Vega.

records.headline: A report on President Heureaux's assassination at Moca says his death caused a panic, that Juan Isidoro Jiminez, who
records.summary_en: A report on President Heureaux's assassination at Moca says his death caused a panic, that Juan Isidoro Jiminez, who took part in the attempted insurrection of the previous year, is a candidate for the presidency, and that General Maximo Gomez is also reported to aspire to it. It notes that the father of Caceres, the assassin, was put to death by order of Heureaux in 1884, that Vice President Wenceslao Figuereo at once assumed the direction of affairs, and that President McKinley sent Figuereo a cable of condolences in the name of the American people.

Señala que el padre de Cáceres, el asesino, fue ejecutado por orden de Heureaux en 1884, que el vicepresidente Wenceslao Figuereo asumió de inmediato la dirección de los asuntos, y que el presidente McKinley envió a Figuereo un cable de condolencias en nombre del pueblo americano.

The father of Caceros, the assassin, was put to death by order of President Heureaux in 1884. Vice President Wenceslao Figuereo, immediately upon the announcement of the president's death, assumed the direction of affairs. It has long been expected that Heureaux would be assassinated. He used to boast that he was a more absolute ruler than any czar or emperor in the world. His ability and shrewdness made a great impression on Europeans and Americans who met him. His daring was remarkable and his shrewdness was said to be equal to that of the most experienced European diplomats. The president was frequently reported assassinated. He had numerous enemies. As a political mystifier he had great talent and boldness. He himself caused reports to be circulated that he had been seized by revolutionists, imprisoned and subsequently shot. This was done to draw out his enemies. When they appeared, Heureaux would ride up, followed by his army, and capture them. They were usually put to death at once. records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Journal* reported on Dominican fiscal measures requiring a portion of customs duties to be paid in paper currency, which would be publicly burned each month to retire the circulating paper notes. Concurrently, Dominican revolutionary forces crossed from Ouanaminthe, Haiti, and captured the border town of Dajabon, forcing the local garrison to retreat to Fort Belair. The report noted expectations that rebel leader General Jimenes would soon land to take direct command, despite Haitian efforts to prevent his transit.
records.summary_es: El *Indianapolis Journal* informó sobre las medidas fiscales dominicanas que exigían el pago de una porción de los aranceles aduaneros en papel moneda, el cual se quemaría públicamente cada mes para retirar los billetes en circulación. Al mismo tiempo, fuerzas revolucionarias dominicanas cruzaron desde Ouanaminthe, Haití, y tomaron la localidad fronteriza de Dajabón, obligando a la guarnición local a replegarse hacia Fort Belair. El informe señalaba la expectativa de que el líder rebelde general Jimenes desembarcara en breve para asumir el mando directo, pese a los esfuerzos haitianos por impedir su paso.

According to a former law now in force a certain part of the export dues is applied for the same purpose. [illegible] — General Francisco Liriano, sent from Monte Christi by the Dominican Government to attack General Ramon Pacheco at Dajabon, the headquarters of the Revolutionists, was abandoned when he arrived in front of the enemy by his troops, who, without firing a shot, deserted and entered the camp of General Pacheco. The advanced post of the latter are at Las Aguas, and the revolutionists are masters of the fords across the river Yaque, thus cutting off communication between Monte Christi and the interior. The forces of Don Juan Isidro Jiminez, leader of the revolutionary forces, are being augmented every day, and the news from all parts of the Dominican republic is favorable to him

records.headline: THEY JOINED THE REBELS’ News from all Ports of the Dominican
records.summary_en: The *Age-Herald* reported that the Dominican revolutionary movement in favor of Juan Isidro Jimenes was expanding rapidly, with the province of La Vega in revolt. Government troops commanded by General Francisco Tiriano deserted en masse upon confronting rebel General Ramon Pacheco at Dajabon, giving the insurgents control of the Yaque River crossings and isolating Monte Cristi. The paper also noted cordial relations between Haiti and the United States, marked by approval for an American meteorological station at Cape Haitien.
records.summary_es: El *Age-Herald* informó que el movimiento revolucionario dominicano en favor de Juan Isidro Jimenes se extendía con rapidez, encontrándose la provincia de La Vega en rebelión. records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Journal* reported that a Dominican revolutionary junta in New York was coordinating with General Juan Isidro Jimenes in Havana to organize expeditions against the Dominican government. Agents Adriano and Maximiliano Grullon worked to mobilize Dominican diaspora communities in New York, Philadelphia, and Boston to back the insurrection. Meanwhile, officials in Santo Domingo reported general tranquillity, though the sixteen conspirators who killed President Heureaux remained at large and the national economy remained paralyzed by currency difficulties.
records.summary_es: El *Indianapolis Journal* informó que una junta revolucionaria dominicana en Nueva York se coordinaba con el general Juan Isidro Jimenes en La Habana para organizar expediciones contra el gobierno dominicano. Los agentes Adriano y Maximiliano Grullón trabajaban para movilizar a las comunidades de la diáspora dominicana en Nueva York, Filadelfia y Boston en apoyo a la insurrección. Entretanto, las autoridades en Santo Domingo informaban de una tranquilidad general, aunque los dieciséis conspiradores que mataron al presidente Heureaux seguían prófugos y la economía nacional permanecía paralizada por dificultades monetarias.
records.passage: A Junto has been formed, which has no official headquarters as yet, but whose members are in conference almost constantly and are supposed to be communicating daily by cable with Gen. Juan Jimenez. The latter, who is still in Havana, is directing the work of the revolutionary forces, and arrangements are understood to be in progress for the sending of expeditions from points in the West Indies and possibly from the United States to aid in the overthrow of the existing government. About fourteen months ago Adriano Grullon, an intimate friend of General Jimenez, came to New York as the representative of the revolutionary party and established close relations with the Dominicans in this city. There are also some natives of Santo Domingo in Boston and Philadelphia whose interest has been enlisted in the cause. About a week ago Mr. Grullon's cousin, Maximiliano Grullon, arrived here from Havana on a secret mission from General Jimenez. Both men held the most confidential relations with the revolutionary leader. Tranquillity Reigns. records.summary_en: The *Passaic City Record* reported that while official tranquillity prevailed in Santo Domingo following President Heureaux's assassination, trade remained depressed due to public reluctance to withdraw paper currency. In addition, a devastating hurricane caused severe flooding and property destruction across San Pedro de Macoris, Samana, and Puerto Plata. In Cuba, American customs officers at Baracoa intercepted an arms shipment of 143 rifles and 18,000 rounds of ammunition bound for Dominican rebels.
records.summary_es: El *Passaic City Record* informó que, si bien prevalecía una aparente tranquilidad en Santo Domingo tras el asesinato del presidente Heureaux, el comercio continuaba deprimido debido a la renuencia del público a aceptar el papel moneda. Además, un devastador huracán provocó graves inundaciones y destrucción material en San Pedro de Macorís, Samaná y Puerto Plata. En Cuba, agentes de aduanas estadounidenses en Baracoa interceptaron un cargamento clandestino de armas de 143 fusiles y 18.000 proyectiles con destino a los rebeldes dominicanos.
records.passage: throughout the country. The assassins of President Heureaux are still at large, but measures have been taken for their capture. It is said the band numbers sixteen. Although the rate for drafts is falling, and there are some signs of returning confidence, business continues dull, and imports are limited. The financial situation is bad. The problem of taking up the paper currency has not yet been solved, as the people in general do not wish it taken up. This is the real cause of dullness in business. Once the matter has been arranged, affairs should take on a different aspect. The latest news from Macoris regarding the effects of the hurricane shows that the damage was more serious than was at first supposed. The river overflowed its banks and inundated the ground. Many families had abandoned their houses for the time and boats were used in the streets to carry people from one point to another. The storm did severe damage in the country about Samana and Puerto Plata. The United States cruiser New Orleans has left San Domingo Harbor for Porto Rico. The United States gunboat Machias is still here. Watch on Filibusters. Twenty-five men, Cubans and Dominicans, arrived by there on board the Mortera. They have been kept under close watch, as they are apparently planning to take arms to San Domingo. records.summary_en: A feature on Santo Domingo describes its minerals, including rock salt, petroleum found near Azua, abundant copper and great masses of iron ore in the interior, and explains that the president is chosen by an electoral college for four years with a cabinet of six. It says sugar, tobacco, cacao and coffee are the leading exports, that the United States led all other countries in trade with the republic, that most sugar estates are owned by Americans with the crop estimated at 65,000 tons, and that steamers of the Samana Bay Fruit Company carry fifteen to eighteen thousand bunches of bananas on each trip to the United States.

Petroleum has been found in the vicinity of Azua, and copper is said by geologists and prospectors to be abundant. There are said also to be great masses of iron ore in the interior, but at such a great distance from any port that they cannot be made available until railroads shall have been built. Other minerals in the Island are silver, platinum, manganese, tin, antimony, marble, coal, and chalcedony. Mineral springs abound. The executive authority is vested in the President, who is chosen by an electoral college, and serves for four years. He is assisted by a Cabinet of six members. There is also a Vice President. records.headline: This account describes the Republic of Santo Domingo, which covers 18,045 of the island's 28,240 square miles, its rivers
records.summary_en: This account describes the Republic of Santo Domingo, which covers 18,045 of the island's 28,240 square miles, its rivers, its gold washings, the rock-salt hills of the Neyba valley, petroleum near Azua and other minerals, and a government headed by a president chosen by an electoral college for four years. Its four leading exports are sugar, tobacco, cacao and coffee; the sugar crop this season is estimated at 65,000 tons and most sugar estates are owned by Americans, tobacco goes chiefly to Germany, and the Samana Bay Fruit Company's steamers carry fifteen to eighteen thousand bunches of bananas on each trip to the United States.
records.summary_es: Esta descripción presenta la República de Santo Domingo, que cubre 18.045 de las 28.240 millas cuadradas de la isla, sus ríos, sus lavaderos de oro, las colinas de sal de roca del valle de Neyba, el petróleo cerca de Azua y otros minerales, y un gobierno encabezado por un presidente elegido por un colegio electoral por cuatro años. Sus cuatro principales productos de exportación son el azúcar, el tabaco, el cacao y el café; la cosecha de azúcar de esta temporada se estima en 65.000 toneladas y la mayoría de las haciendas azucareras son propiedad de americanos, el tabaco va principalmente a Alemania, y los vapores de la Samana Bay Fruit Company llevan de quince a dieciocho mil racimos de plátanos en cada viaje a los Estados Unidos.
records.passage: by Americans. English, French, German and Italian capital is also invested in this industry. Tobacco is extensively grown and much of it is said to be of a quality nearly equal to the celebrated Havana product. Germany is the chief market for this crop. The banana industry is a growing one. The steamers of the Samana Bay Fruit Company make three or four trips a month to the United States, and on each trip between fifteen and eighteen thousand bunches of the fruit are carried. Mahogany, lignum vitae, logwood, honey, wax, hides, fruits, and sugar are exported almost exclusively to this country, while the coffee, cocoa and tobacco find their market in Germany and other European countries. THE BISHOP A BORROWER. Church Mortgages to Be Raised With English Money. New York, Aug. 19—Bishop Wigger, of the Catholic Diocese of Newark, has confirmed the report that he proposes to accept a loan of $1,500,000 from an English syndicate to be used in taking up mortgages on the churches in his diocese, upon which 5 per cent interest is exacted. Under the new arrangement only 3 1-2 per cent interest will be charged by the foreign syndicate. The Bishop of Madison yesterday said he would probably have the money next week. It is estimated that Catholic Church property in this diocese, which is worth about 10,000,000, is mortgaged for nearly $2,000,000. The syndicate considers the property gilt-edged security, and is willing to advance another million if the loan of $1,500,000 does not prove sufficient.

records.summary_en: A Puerto Plata dispatch dated September 1 reports that President Figuereo of the Dominican Republic has abdicated, yielding his authority to his council of ministers, and that the revolution in favor of Jiminez is victorious. It describes how Puerto Plata was handed over to the revolutionary generals without a drop of blood being shed, amid flags, music and public celebration, and how the revolutionists had also established a provisional government at Santiago with General Vasquez as president and General Caceres as minister of war.

Describe cómo Puerto Plata fue entregada a los generales revolucionarios sin que se derramara una gota de sangre, entre banderas, música y celebración pública, y cómo los revolucionarios también habían establecido un gobierno provisional en Santiago con el general Vásquez como presidente y el general Cáceres como ministro de Guerra.

A civic procession, representing all classes of the population, did honor to the patriotism and honesty of General Cocco and former Governor Emilio Gordero. records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Journal* reported the capture of major Dominican northern cities by revolutionary forces, including the surrender of Puerto Plata on August 26. Insurgent troops stormed and took the military fort at Santiago de los Caballeros during the night of August 27 after garrison officials rejected surrender terms. On August 28, civil authorities in Puerto Plata formally transferred power to revolutionary leaders General Imbert and General Garrido in a public ceremony witnessed by foreign consuls and celebratory crowds.
records.summary_es: El *Indianapolis Journal* informó sobre la toma de las principales ciudades del norte dominicano por fuerzas revolucionarias, incluida la rendición de Puerto Plata el 26 de agosto. Tropas insurgentes asaltaron y capturaron la fortaleza militar de Santiago de los Caballeros durante la noche del 27 de agosto, luego de que los mandos de la guarnición rechazaran las condiciones de capitulación. El 28 de agosto, las autoridades civiles de Puerto Plata transfirieron formalmente el poder a los líderes revolucionarios, el general Imbert y el general Garrido, en una ceremonia pública presenciada por cónsules extranjeros y multitudes en júbilo.
records.passage: Puerto Plata, looking to its instant surrender. The city surrendered Aug. 26. The part of the revolutionary army besieging the city of Santiago de los Caballeros demanded its surrender. Its officials refused to consider proposals, and the revolutionists attacked and captured the city. Negotiations were opened for a surrender of the fort. The terms were declined, and the revolutionary forces attacked the fort during the night of Aug. 27, and the place was taken by storm. After the capture of the fort the officer who is in command of the government troops entertained the victors. The casualties of the revolutionary army number one officer and six men wounded. Guarantees were given Garrido and Villaverde, who are now tranquilly reposing at their residences. records.summary_en: Writing from San Domingo on September 15, the Herald's correspondent reports that the assassination of President Heureaux removed the hand that had for eighteen years preserved a bloody peace, and that Vice President Figuereo's government weakened as he hesitated to dismiss the Heureaux ministry. Late in August a revolutionary proclamation was issued at San Francisco de Macoris in the interest of Jimenez, telegraph communication was cut, and the correspondent reports that Macoris, Moca and La Vega went over to a revolution headed by Horacio Vasquez, Ramon Caceres and Samuel Mayo.

A fines de agosto se emitió una proclama revolucionaria en San Francisco de Macorís en favor de Jiménez, se cortó la comunicación telegráfica, y el corresponsal informa que Macorís, Moca y La Vega se pasaron a una revolución encabezada por Horacio Vásquez, Ramón Cáceres y Samuel Mayo.

records.full_text:
MEETS FRENCH ADMIRAL.

Jimenez Confers With Richard—Settlement Expected To-Day.

SPECIAL BY CABLE.
Santo Domingo, Jan. 9.—(Copyright, 1900, by James Gordon Bennett.)—Admiral Richard of the French navy, with his staff, formally called upon President Jimenez this morning. No business was transacted. The French Consul was present. It is rumored on good authority that the French Consul has not been sustained by his Government, and that he has been asked for his resignation.

It is expected that official action will be taken to-morrow. Americans of this place have asked the United States not to allow France to dictate terms to the Dominican Government. An American cruiser is expected to arrive to-day. One is reported to have left Sanchez yesterday.

ORDERS TO THE MACHIAS.
REPUBLIC SPECIAL.
Washington, Jan. 9.—Instructions were to-day cabled to Commander L. C. Logan, commanding the Machias, directing him to promptly return to Santo Domingo.

In compliance with this instruction, it is presumed the Machias has left San Juan bound for the capital of Santo Domingo. Upon his arrival Commander Logan will consult with the American Minister relative to the protection of American interests. It was said at the State Department this evening that no appeal for the intervention of the United States had been received from Santo Domingo and it is hardly likely that this Government will interfere, in view of the fact that the Jimenez Government has collected by popular subscription the money necessary to pay the French claims. It is possible that Minister Powell may act as a mediator between the French fleet and President Jimenez, looking to compliance with the French demand for an apology, but now that the money has been collected [illegible] [illegible] believed that the worst is about over.

records.headline: Admiral Richard of the French navy is not de manding money
records.summary_en: The *Chariton Courier* reported that French Admiral Richard concurred with the Dominican government's position on the Boismare-Caccavelli claims dispute and accepted the terms previously proposed by Dominican authorities. The Dominican government secured a loan to satisfy the financial claim, releasing citizens from the funds collected by popular subscription. Meanwhile, the French warship *Suchet* departed for Haiti to collect 200,000 francs connected to a secret border agreement negotiated with the late President Heureaux.
records.summary_es: El *Chariton Courier* informó que el almirante francés Richard coincidió con la postura del gobierno dominicano respecto a la controversia por las reclamaciones Boismare-Caccavelli y aceptó los términos propuestos con anterioridad por las autoridades dominicanas. El gobierno dominicano obtuvo un préstamo para saldar la reclamación financiera, liberando a los ciudadanos de los fondos reunidos por suscripción popular. Entretanto, el buque de guerra francés *Suchet* zarpó hacia Haití para cobrar 200.000 francos vinculados a un acuerdo fronterizo secreto negociado con el difunto presidente Heureaux.
records.passage: Disputed Claim. Santo Domingo, Jan. 16. — The French admiral finds on investigation of all facts that the Dominican government was correct in its attitude on the Boismare-Caccavelli claim. Admiral Richard of the French navy is not demanding money, but he has accepted the terms which the Dominican government proposed to the French consul before his protest. The Dominican government, having contracted a loan, prefers to pay the amount of the claim, and will thank the people of the republic for the popular subscription, which will not be used. It is probable that the French consul will be recalled soon. The French warship Suchet has left for Haiti in order to enforce the payment of 200,000 francs paid to the late President Heureaux for lands never ceded, as provided in the secret settlement of the boundary questions. Kruger Still Confident. Pretoria, Thursday, Jan. 11, via Lourenco Marques. — President Kruger, in the course of a stirring address just issued to the burghers, affirms that providence is on their side, that their cause is just and that they must succeed. To Be Tried as Rebels. Cape Town, Jan. 16. — Col. Pilcher's prisoners will be tried as rebels, it is understood, before the Supreme court, as the military authorities have no jurisdiction, martial law not having been proclaimed in Cape Colony.

records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Journal* reported on diplomatic friction in Santo Domingo arising from the French consul's abrupt demand on December 5 for immediate installment payments on the Boismare-Caccavelli claims. Dominican citizens held public meetings to protest the consul's haste, while carefully avoiding anti-French hostility. Foreign Minister Henríquez y Carvajal responded to consular complaints on January 4, defending the dignified conduct of the Dominican populace and reaffirming friendship with France.
records.summary_es: El *Indianapolis Journal* informó sobre las tensiones diplomáticas en Santo Domingo surgidas por la abrupta exigencia del cónsul francés el 5 de diciembre para el pago inmediato de cuotas por las reclamaciones Boismare-Caccavelli. Los ciudadanos dominicanos celebraron asambleas públicas para protestar contra la premura del cónsul, evitando con cautela cualquier hostilidad antifrancesa. records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported further statements by Judge Durham concerning the collapse of the Dominican currency system under late President Heureaux. Durham disclosed that Heureaux systematically evaded agreements with the San Domingo Improvement Company by shifting printing plates between American firms to produce excessive quantities of unauthorized paper money. This unchecked currency inflation created widespread commercial distrust, leaving the Improvement Company with large unusable balances and bringing local commerce to an abrupt standstill upon the president's death.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó sobre declaraciones adicionales del juez Durham relativas al colapso del sistema monetario dominicano bajo el mandato del difunto presidente Heureaux. Durham reveló que Heureaux eludía sistemáticamente los convenios con la San Domingo Improvement Company transfiriendo matrices de impresión entre compañías estadounidenses para fabricar cantidades excesivas de papel moneda sin autorización. Esta inflación monetaria desmedida generó una desconfianza comercial generalizada, dejando a la Improvement Company con abultados saldos inutilizables y paralizando repentinamente el comercio local tras el deceso del mandatario.

The issue was authorized by the San Domingo Improvement Company to the extent of about a million, but when the President began the issue he had control of the plates and went on issuing. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that President McKinley received the credentials of the new Dominican Envoy Extraordinary and Minister Plenipotentiary at the White House. In his address, the Dominican minister emphasized the historical friendship between both nations and advocated concluding a reciprocal commercial treaty. President McKinley welcomed the envoy and reciprocated the desire to establish closer, mutually beneficial trade relations between the two republics.

records.summary_en: Washington reported on January 12 that the government would probably take cognizance of the troubles in San Domingo and act as necessary for the protection of American interests, but that the State Department had not yet heard from Consul-General Maxwell on the reports that the Dominican Government had resumed the direction of its own fiscal affairs, terminating the system by which an American syndicate collected the duties and paid the debts of the government. The plan had been adopted some years earlier, and some Belgian bond owners were understood to have objected to it. Representatives of the San Domingo Improvement Company held long conferences with Acting Secretary Hill and Solicitor Penfield concerning the reported repudiation of the companys grant, and a cable message of inquiry was sent to the American representative in San Domingo.
records.summary_es: Washington informó el 12 de enero de que el gobierno probablemente tomaría conocimiento de los problemas en Santo Domingo y actuaría según fuera necesario para proteger los intereses estadounidenses, pero que el Departamento de Estado aún no había recibido noticias del cónsul general Maxwell sobre los informes de que el gobierno dominicano había reasumido la dirección de sus propios asuntos fiscales, poniendo fin al sistema por el que un sindicato estadounidense cobraba los derechos y pagaba las deudas del gobierno. El plan se había adoptado años antes, y se entendía que algunos tenedores de bonos belgas habían objetado a él. Representantes de la San Domingo Improvement Company celebraron largas conferencias con el secretario interino Hill y el procurador Penfield sobre la supuesta rescisión de la concesión de la compañía, y se envió un cable de consulta al representante estadounidense en Santo Domingo.
records.passage: Washington, Jan. 12.—The Government probably will take cognizance of the troubles in San Domingo and will take such action as is necessary for the protection of American interests there. Thus far, however, the State Department has not heard from Consul-General Maxwell on the reports that the Dominican Government has resumed the direction of its own fiscal affairs, thus terminating the system by which an American syndicate collected the duties and paid the debts of the Government. records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Journal* reported that the United States State Department requested an urgent report from Consul General Maxwell regarding the Dominican government's reported termination of the San Domingo Improvement Company's contract. Meanwhile, dispatches from Santo Domingo indicated that the Dominican Congress had voted compensation for the American firm while resuming direct customs administration. Customs receipts were placed under the supervision of a joint commission representing Dutch, Belgian, French, American, and Dominican officials.
records.summary_es: El *Indianapolis Journal* informó que el Departamento de Estado de los Estados Unidos solicitó un informe urgente al cónsul general Maxwell respecto a la presunta rescisión del contrato de la San Domingo Improvement Company por parte del gobierno dominicano. Mientras tanto, despachos procedentes de Santo Domingo indicaban que el Congreso dominicano había votado una indemnización para la firma estadounidense al tiempo que reasumía la administración aduanera directa. La recaudación aduanera quedó bajo la supervisión de una comisión conjunta en representación de funcionarios holandeses, belgas, franceses, estadounidenses y dominicanos.

records.summary_en: The *Savannah Morning News* reported that the Santo Domingo Chamber of Commerce passed a resolution repudiating the San Domingo Improvement Company's attempt to declare government customs collections invalid. The commercial body demanded that the American company rescind its provocative notice to merchants. In response to the escalating dispute, the Dominican Minister of Foreign Affairs prepared to travel to Washington to present his government's case directly to the United States.
records.summary_es: El *Savannah Morning News* informó que la Cámara de Comercio de Santo Domingo aprobó una resolución desconociendo la pretensión de la San Domingo Improvement Company de declarar inválida la recaudación aduanera gubernamental. La entidad comercial exigió que la compañía estadounidense revocara su provocador aviso a los comerciantes. Ante la escalada del conflicto, el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores de la República Dominicana se dispuso a viajar a Washington para exponer los argumentos de su gobierno directamente ante los Estados Unidos.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published an interview with Dominican leader Horacio Vásquez, who described the nation's abundant mineral resources, including deposits of copper, precious metals, and vast salt reserves. Vásquez maintained that political stability had been quickly restored after President Heureaux's assassination through the establishment of a provisional government. He sharply criticized the San Domingo Improvement Company, asserting that it had merely constructed a railroad with Dominican state funds, enriching itself, Heureaux, and local financier Cosme Batlle at the country's expense.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* publicó una entrevista con el líder dominicano Horacio Vásquez, quien describió los abundantes recursos minerales de la nación, incluidos yacimientos de cobre, metales preciosos y vastas reservas de sal. Vásquez sostuvo que la estabilidad política se restableció con rapidez tras el asesinato del presidente Heureaux mediante la constitución de un gobierno provisional. Criticó duramente a la San Domingo Improvement Company, aseverando que únicamente había construido un ferrocarril con fondos del Estado dominicano, enriqueciéndose a sí misma, a Heureaux y al financista local Cosme Batlle a expensas del país.
records.passage: conditions are procured. The natural resources of the country are rich. We have there mines of all kinds-gold, silver, tin. copper, salt. There is a whole mountain of salt, waiting to be carried away. The business of the country is flourishing. The revolution did not disturb it. There were not enough revolutions to do it. The president was killed, and there was disorder for a few days; then the people from all parts of the country flocked to Vasquez and formed the provisional government." Senor Vasquez was asked regarding the San Domingo Improvement Company, an American concern which undertook to finance the new republic, and is now having trouble with the Dominican government on account of the government's refusal to allow it longer to collect the customs duties. "The San Domingo Improvement Company." said Senor Vasquez, "has done nothing except build a railroad. This it did with government money. But when the road was in working order President Heureaux presented it to the company, and the proceeds were pocketed by three parties: the company, President Heureaux and Cosine Battle, a rich man of San Domingo, who advanced money to the company when it went to San Domingo without a cent of capital." records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported that nationalist pressure compelled President Jimenes to confront the San Domingo Improvement Company and threaten its agent with expulsion after the company challenged Dominican customs authority. Meanwhile, Belgian Foreign Minister de Favereau instructed his consul in Santo Domingo to ensure that bondholder funds in the treasury safe remained strictly protected for European creditors. Additionally, the semi-official Dominican press responded defiantly to rumors that the American gunboat *Scorpion* was en route to coerce the government.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó que presiones nacionalistas obligaron al presidente Jimenes a confrontar a la San Domingo Improvement Company y a amenazar a su agente con la expulsión después de que la empresa desafiara la autoridad aduanera dominicana. Mientras tanto, el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores belga, De Favereau, instruyó a su cónsul en Santo Domingo para que garantizara que los fondos de los tenedores de bonos en la caja fuerte de la tesorería permanecieran estrictamente resguardados para los acreedores europeos. Asimismo, la prensa semioficial dominicana respondió con desafío a los rumores de que el cañonero estadounidense *Scorpion* se dirigía a coaccionar al gobierno.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported the arrival in New York of Dr. Francisco Henríquez y Carvajal, the Dominican Minister of Foreign Affairs, aboard the steamer *San Juan*. Serving as a special commissioner appointed by President Jimenes, Henríquez traveled to present his government's position to the State Department in Washington. His mission aimed to resolve the acute diplomatic controversy surrounding the Dominican Republic's termination of its contract with the San Domingo Improvement Company.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó sobre la llegada a Nueva York del Dr. Francisco Henríquez y Carvajal, ministro de Relaciones Exteriores dominicano, a bordo del vapor *San Juan*. En calidad de comisionado especial designado por el presidente Jimenes, Henríquez viajó para exponer la postura de su gobierno ante el Departamento de Estado en Washington. Su misión tenía como objetivo resolver la grave controversia diplomática en torno a la rescisión contractual por parte de la República Dominicana con la San Domingo Improvement Company.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Belgian envoy Willem Willems presented the State Department with legal credentials representing 3,619 European bondholders holding over twelve million dollars in Dominican bonds. Willems informed American officials that the European bondholders supported the Dominican government in its dispute with the San Domingo Improvement Company. He argued that the contract granting the American syndicate control over customs revenues was legally invalid because it was never ratified by the bondholders as required.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el enviado belga Willem Willems presentó ante el Departamento de Estado credenciales legales en representación de 3.619 tenedores de bonos europeos poseedores de más de doce millones de dólares en bonos dominicanos. Willems comunicó a los funcionarios estadounidenses que los tenedores de bonos europeos respaldaban al gobierno dominicano en su disputa con la San Domingo Improvement Company. Sostuvo que el contrato que otorgaba al consorcio estadounidense el control sobre los ingresos aduaneros carecía de validez legal por no haber sido nunca ratificado por los tenedores de bonos conforme se exigía.

Mr. Willems explained to Acting Secretary Hill and Solicitor Penfield, who are considering this case, that all the original bonds had been deposited by their owners In the banks of Antwerp, Brussels and Amsterdam. All of these bondholders are siding with the Dominican government in its contest with the improvement company. According to Mr. Willems' statement, the bondholders insist that the last contract made between the Dominican government and the Improvement company, farming out the revenues, was nullified by the fact that it lacked the assent of the bondholders, a condition imposed by the Dominican government at the time the contract was drawn. records.summary_en: The *San Antonio Daily Light* reported rising tensions along the Haitian-Dominican border following the failure of a joint boundary commission established under the Sam-Heureaux convention. Haitian authorities accused Dominican forces of illegally occupying frontier positions that Haitian troops had evacuated in good faith to facilitate negotiations. Violent skirmishes erupted at Philobert along the Massacre River, where Haitian border posts established to suppress smuggling came under repeated Dominican attack.
records.summary_es: El *San Antonio Daily Light* informó sobre el aumento de las tensiones en la frontera domínico-haitiana tras el fracaso de una comisión mixta de límites creada en el marco de la convención Sam-Heureaux. Las autoridades haitianas acusaron a las fuerzas dominicanas de ocupar ilegalmente puestos fronterizos que las tropas haitianas habían desalojado de buena fe para facilitar las negociaciones. Estallaron violentas escaramuzas en Philobert a lo largo del río Masacre, donde los puestos fronterizos haitianos establecidos para reprimir el contrabando fueron objeto de reiterados ataques dominicanos.

records.summary_en: The *Morning Astorian* reported on the breakdown of the joint boundary commission that convened at Anses-à-Pitres to define the Haitian-Dominican border based on 1874 territorial positions. Negotiations collapsed after Dominican delegates insisted on conditional compliance and Dominican troops moved into vacated frontier points, prompting Haitian accusations of bad faith. Tensions escalated sharply following armed confrontations at Philobert near the Massacre River, where Haitian border outposts repelled attacks from Dominican territory.

Las negociaciones fracasaron luego de que los delegados dominicanos insistieran en un cumplimiento condicional y las tropas dominicanas avanzaran hacia puntos fronterizos desocupados, lo que motivó acusaciones haitianas de mala fe. Las tensiones se intensificaron bruscamente tras choques armados en Philobert, cerca del río Masacre, donde los puestos fronterizos haitianos repelieron ataques procedentes de territorio dominicano.

records.headline: The patriots won, the Spaniards were forced to capitulate, and Gomez
records.summary_en: The *Phillipsburg Herald* reviewed the military career of General Máximo Gómez, noting his early service with Spanish forces during the Dominican annexation before becoming a leader in Cuba's ten years' war for independence. In 1887, Gómez returned to Santo Domingo to cultivate tobacco in Guayubín near Monte Cristi, where his widespread popularity quickly aroused political suspicion. Fearing that Gómez harbored presidential ambitions and planned an insurrection, President Heureaux secretly arranged for his arrest and execution.
records.summary_es: El *Phillipsburg Herald* repasó la carrera militar del general Máximo Gómez, destacando su servicio inicial en las fuerzas españolas durante la anexión dominicana antes de convertirse en un caudillo de la guerra de los Diez Años por la independencia de Cuba. En 1887, Gómez regresó a Santo Domingo para cultivar tabaco en Guayubín, cerca de Monte Cristi, donde su inmensa popularidad despertó pronto suspicacias políticas. Por temor a que Gómez albergara ambiciones presidenciales y tramara una insurrección, el presidente Heureaux dispuso secretamente su arresto y ejecución.

Santana, of [Cibao?], Gomez, then a young and brave soldier, allied his destinies with the annexationists. 'When the war of the restoration began he took sides with the Spaniards instead of the patriots. The patriots won, the Spaniards were forced to capitulate, and Gomez, with other Dominicans, retired to Havana, with the title of Mariscal de Campo. "Gomez soon grew tired of Spanish rule, and when the ten years' war for Cuban independence began, under the leadership of Maceo and others, Gomez was one of the leading spirits who battled for Cuban independence. Private advices from Guayabin announced that Gomez was aspiring to the presidency, and an uprising was imminent to usurp the reins of the government. The oppositionists began to be so active that Gen. Heureaux was seriously concerned, and the imprisonment and execution of Gomez were planned.

records.summary_en: The *Arizona Republican* reported that Dominican insurgents captured the southern coastal town of Barahona after heavy fighting that resulted in forty casualties. A government gunboat subsequently bombarded the port and landed forces that successfully recaptured the town, driving the rebels into nearby strongholds. In response to the uprising, the Dominican Congress suspended constitutional guarantees and declared nationwide martial law.
records.summary_es: El *Arizona Republican* informó que insurgentes dominicanos tomaron la localidad costera meridional de Barahona tras intensos combates que causaron cuarenta bajas. Con posterioridad, un cañonero gubernamental bombardeó el puerto y desembarcó tropas que recuperaron con éxito la ciudad, obligando a los rebeldes a replegarse hacia reductos cercanos. En respuesta a la sublevación, el Congreso dominicano suspendió las garantías constitucionales y declaró la ley marcial en todo el territorio nacional.
records.passage: Insurgent Gains Government Puts Island Under Martial Law. San Domingo, Republic of Santo Domingo, March 31. The town of Barahona, on the south coast, was attacked and captured by revolutionists after a severe fight in which forty were killed or wounded. Later a government gunboat bombarded Barahona and landed troops, who retook the town. The revolutionists retired to a stronghold in the neighborhood. The Dominican minister of war proceeded to Barahona with other troops and will take severe measures to re-establish order. Revolutionary activity is for the present confined to Barahona. The Dominican congress has declared that martial law shall be established throughout the whole republic and that constitutional guarantees be suspended. FROM DULUTH TO THE GULF Funds Raised for a Road to Cut "All Trans-Continental Lines. Duluth, Minn.. March 31. The News- Tribune publishes a statement to the effect that the banques Francaise and Colonial of Paris and Belgium have agreed to take $12,000,000 of the bonds for the building of the Manitoba Gulf railroad on a basis of 95 per cent. The road will run from Duluth to Omaha and Kansas City, cutting every one of the great trans-continental lines. It is the intentions of the promoters to either make connections with the Gould interests or continue the road as an independent line to the gulf. Work will commence immediately.

records.summary_en: The paper reports another revolution was said to have broken out in Santo Domingo, with telegraphic communication interrupted and Santiago as the center of disturbance led by Vice President Horacio Vásquez, though it was believed government forces would suppress it. A U.S. gunboat report from Barahona said there was no excitement ashore and insurgents had about 200 men against about 500 government troops.

Un informe de un cañonero estadounidense desde Barahona dijo que no había agitación en tierra y que los insurgentes tenían unos 200 hombres frente a unos 500 soldados gubernamentales.
