records.full_text:
REPORT STATES BOSS OF HAITI FINDS ALL O. K.

By Louis R. Lautier

During the past year the American treaty officials have been directing their efforts toward increasing the productive wealth of Haiti to the ultimate end of strengthening and improving the general economic condition, Brig. Gen. John H. Russell, American High Commissioner to Haiti, declared in his fifth annual report to the Secretary of State, which was made public by the State Department Monday.

In addition, he reported, the Haitian Government and the treaty officials have continued the general governing program for the stablization of Haitian finances, the maintenance of law and order, the construction of public works, and the improvement of the public health service.

A bumper coffee crop in a period of exceptionally high and abnormal prices and the re-election

BOSS OF HAITI REPORTS EVERYTHING IS O. K.

(Continued from page 1)

of President Borno contributed to the stability and the prosperity of Haiti in 1926, General Russell stated.

Business Confidence
“Confidence among business men, which, on account of the usual sensational rumors which precede a presidential election in Haiti, had been trembling in the balance, was restored immediately upon the promulgation of the results of the election,” General Russell reports. “This fact contributed largely in making the past year the greatest in the history of the Republic from a financial and business point of view.”

As a result of the visit of President Borno to the United States in last June he returned to Haiti imbued with a stronger desire to further the progress and development of his country and to make it a republic in being as well as in name, General Russell states.

The Haitian judiciary system is in need of complete renovation. “The courts are, if such could be possible, less effective than ever and their inefficiency and incompetency more notorious,” General Russell reports. “Trials by jury are farcial.”

There has been no reduction in the United States forces in Haiti. They consist of a skeleton brigade of United States marines and a mine sweeper of 950 tons displacement. Martial law has only been exercised upon the rarest occasions, says General Russell.

The customs receipts for the past year were unprecedented. The total receipts amounted to $9,072,929.62. Of this amount the sum of $8,118,996.35 was from custom revenues.

The Public Debt
The actual debt reducing amortization was $1,384,836.90. The required reduction was only $717,218.36. The total public debt amounts to $18,849,000.

As a result of the favorable year just closed the Haitian people have been benefited materially, says General Russell. They are better fed, better clothed, and better housed than ever before.

The commerce of Haiti during the past year has been most satisfactory, it is reported. There has been a healthy growth of shipping entering the harbors of the Republic and a gradual increase in traffic across the Dominican border.

Educational Ideas
The Haitian Government believes that its educational system should be designed to furnish agricultural education to the rural and industrial education to the urban population, the American high commissioner states. He says that “the Haitian Government considers it not only essential but vital that the Haitian people be taught to use their hands.”

General Russell also states in his report:
“The efforts that have been made and are being made to foster the further increase of production in Haiti will soon show results and with the passing of an appropriate revenue law and the renovation of the Haitian judiciary, the advance toward the stabilization of government will be most marked.

“As in past years President Borno has co-operated in every way for the carrying out of the provisions of the treaty of 1915, and has made the marked improvement of last year possible.

“The treaty officials have consistently, tactfully and energetically carried out their duties and the efficient management of the respective departments under their control has largely contributed to the remarkable progress which is being made in the bringing of happiness and prosperity to the Haitian people.”

Statements Contradictory
Statements in the report of General Russell are contradictory to those made upon the floor of the Senate by Senator William H. King, Democrat, of Utah, who was recently barred by President Borno from visiting Haiti because of derogatory remarks made by the Senator concerning the Haitian president in demanding that the American forces be withdrawn from the island republic.

In a speech in the Senate on February 1 last, Senator King declared:
“First, let it be remembered that by every standard of morality and justice there was no treaty. Our forces were in possession of the country. We had destroyed the legislative branch of the government and taken possession of all governmental agencies of the country. We set up a shadow government. It was not a Haitian government. A few Haitians were put into positions, but they were named by Naval officers of the United States and they did the will of those who named them. One of them we called a President, and he was required to sign a treaty prepared by the United States.”

Senator King described the re-election of President Borno as a farce. This “shadow president,” he said, was chosen by members of an assembly which he had appointed. “The Haitian people,” he declared, “are in a condition of political servitude.”

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that U.S. Senator William H. King, upon returning from the Caribbean, denounced Haitian President Borno as a puppet of the State Department and High Commissioner General John H. Russell. King produced official correspondence showing that Borno's order barring him from Haiti was enforced through American military officers, arguing that U.S. claims of Haitian sovereignty were a subterfuge. The senator vowed to renew his fight in Congress to withdraw American marines, asserting that 89 percent of Haitians opposed the occupation.

King presentó correspondencia oficial que demostraba que la orden de Borno de impedirle la entrada a Haití fue ejecutada por oficiales militares estadounidenses, argumentando que las afirmaciones de Washington sobre la soberanía haitiana eran un subterfugio. El senador prometió renovar su lucha en el Congreso para retirar a los infantes de marina, asegurando que el 89 por ciento de los haitianos se oponía a la ocupación.

S. [illegible], American officer in charge of the gendarmerie in Haiti, and copies of correspondence showing that the order to exclude him had been referred to Gen. "The attitude of the State Department," the Senator said, "regarding the exclusion incident indicates that it was an effort to keep alive the fiction of Haitien independence. Mr. Knowles said that the policies and acts presented were not those of the American people, nor even of the American Congress, but of the American government, which notwithstanding the fact that only Congress can declare war, had committed acts of war in these republics by the landing of armed forces. Northampton, Nov. 21 — The two buildings occupied by J. E. Lambie Co. of Main street, and the stock of dry goods, suits and coats, were destroyed by fire this morning at 4, and there were heavy losses on the furniture stock of J. H. Quinn, and the block occupied by Quinn, owned by J. H. O'Dea, and smaller losses on the clothing stocks of M. J. Keating, on one side of the Lambie store, and Coffey Burke in the other side. The present owners of Lambie Co. are George F. Edwards and James P. Fairchild. The losses, as insurance men figure them, probably are not more than $250,000, but replacement values at present high costs of building construction might add another $50,000 to the estimate of total loss.

records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* criticized President Coolidge's speech in Havana, where he asserted that nations including Haiti, Nicaragua, and the Dominican Republic were best suited to govern themselves and make their own mistakes. The editorial argued that this rhetoric contradicted the administration's active military interventions, including aerial bombing in Nicaragua and persistent intervention rights in Cuba.

records.passage: United States is sovereign in this hemisphere. In the closing passages of the address the President vaguely refers to an "international system" peculiar to this hemisphere, which imposes on each nation certain "obligations," "defined by laws which we recognize as binding on all of us." What "laws" there are of the character referred to no one may know, inasmuch as the Monroe doctrine, even with its corollaries stretched to their most extreme imperialistic implication, remains a policy of the United States like Great Britain's old claim to dominate the high seas. Ignoring the realistic bases of the policy of the United States since the Spanish war, the President found himself able to say with perfect gravity, "We are thoroughly committed to the principle that they (the Colombias, Costa Ricas, Haytis, Nicaraguas, Panamas, Dominican Republics and Cubas) are better fitted to govern themselves than anyone else is to govern them. It is better for the people to make their own mistakes than to have someone else make their mistakes for them." Why, then, do we not clear out of the Philippine islands? Even in Cuba, why do we insist on special rights of intervention? Why are our gallant marines put to such work as bombing Nicaraguan villages? There is reason to suspect that two Coolidges were struggling for expression in the Havana address. records.summary_en: Col. Charles A. Lindbergh took off from Santo Domingo at 11 a.m. on February 6 for Port-au-Prince, Haiti, on a 160-mile route flown entirely across land, as he neared the end of his goodwill flight to the Pan American conference at Havana. The night before, he had been guest of honor at a brilliant ball at the presidential palace, attended by the diplomatic body, members of the government and prominent society figures.
records.summary_es: El coronel Charles A. Lindbergh despegó de Santo Domingo a las 11 de la mañana del 6 de febrero rumbo a Puerto Príncipe, Haití, en una ruta de 160 millas volada enteramente sobre tierra, cuando se acercaba al final de su vuelo de buena voluntad a la conferencia panamericana de La Habana. La noche anterior había sido el invitado de honor en un brillante baile en el palacio presidencial, al que asistieron el cuerpo diplomático, miembros del gobierno y destacadas figuras de la sociedad.
records.passage: By the Associated Press. SANTO DOMINGO, Dominican Republic, February 6. — Col. Charles A. Lindbergh, now nearing the end of his good will flight to the Pan American conference at Havana, took off for Port-au-Prince, Haiti, at 11 a.m., local time. The route to Port-au-Prince, 160 miles by airplane from here, led entirely across land, unless Lindbergh in his flight should venture across the inland waters of Lake Enriquillo and Lake Saumatre. The path of the lone eagle was over a country teeming with bird life, wild duck, flamingo, herons and other shore birds. The route passed over mountains and deep forests where voodooism was brought from Africa and practiced for many years. It led over a land where negro slaves by their own efforts freed themselves and set up a republic, of which Port-au-Prince is the capital. Haiti is the second country to be visited by Col. Lindbergh in his good will tour where American Marines are present. In Nicaragua he found them engaged in an active campaign against the rebel Gen. Sandino. In Haiti they are engaged in maintaining order until the new republic is considered capable of exercising in full its rights of sovereignty. Col. Lindbergh was kept busy until late last night. He was the guest of honor at a brilliant ball held at the presidential palace, which was decorated with flowers and lights. All the diplomatic body, members of the Government and prominent society figures attended. CITY WILL HONOR COSTES AND LEBRIX French Flyers, Due Here Tomorrow

The royal commission on customs and excise has recommended to the Canadian government a number of important changes in the Dominion law to facilitate co-operation with the United States authorities to prevent liquor smuggling into this country. records.headline: Commemoration of Great Haitian Liberator's Birth
records.summary_en: The birthday of Toussaint L'Ouverture was commemorated at a memorial meeting in New York under the auspices of the American Negro Labor Congress, with Richard B. Moore acting as chairman. Moore said that a little more than a hundred years after Haiti's triumphant struggle against Napoleon for complete independence, the island found itself under American imperialism, a foreign control he called far more menacing and crushing than the political control of one state over another. The meeting heard that L'Ouverture was born enslaved in the French colony of Haiti, then known as Santo Domingo, overthrew slavery throughout the island and carried on the struggle against Napoleon's reaction, making way for the birth of the republic of Haiti.
records.summary_es: El cumpleaños de Toussaint L'Ouverture fue conmemorado en una reunión memorial en Nueva York, bajo los auspicios del Congreso Americano de Trabajadores Negros, con Richard B. Moore como presidente del acto. Moore declaró que poco más de cien años después de la lucha triunfante de Haití contra Napoleón por su independencia completa, la isla se encontraba bajo el imperialismo estadounidense, un control extranjero que calificó de mucho más amenazante y aplastante que el control político de un Estado sobre otro. En la reunión se recordó que L'Ouverture nació esclavo en la colonia francesa de Haití, entonces conocida como Santo Domingo, abolió la esclavitud en toda la isla y continuó la lucha contra la reacción de Napoleón, abriendo el camino al nacimiento de la república de Haití.

Mr. Moore said a little more than a hundred years after Haiti's triumphant struggle against Napoleon for her complete independence, this island of the West Indies finds itself under the steel heels of American imperialism; a foreign control far more menacing and crushing and deadening than ever attended the political control of one state over another. Toussaint L'Ouverture was born a slave in the French colony of Haiti, then known as Santo Domingo. When the revolution came in France at the close of the eighteenth century the revolutionary ideas of Danton and Robespierre found ready recruits among the toiling slaves and discontented mulattoes of the oppressed island. L'Ouverture was the foremost of the Santo Dominican leaders. He not only overthrew slavery throughout the island but carried on a successful struggle against Napoleon's Thermidorian policy of reaction and made way for the birth of the republic of Haiti, according to the records contained in Chaplain T. G. Steward's History of the Republic of Haiti. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reviewed historical instances of U.S. supervision of Caribbean elections, citing American oversight of Dominican congressional elections in 1913 and presidential elections in 1914. In 1913 the elections for the national assembly of Santo Domingo were supervised by a North American commission. In 1914 the presidential elections were supervised by civil and military representatives. In November, 1916, the United States intervened in the affairs of the Dominican Republic to re-establish order. The republic was then occupied by military forces and no elections were held until 1924. No direct supervision was made of the 1924 elections, although there still remained a few of Uncle Sam's forces and they were observed very closely by a United States representative. records.summary_en: The *Daily Worker* criticized former Vice President Charles G. Dawes's financial mission to Santo Domingo, characterizing it as an imperialist survey designed to secure additional American loans and control. The article noted that Dominican customs had been managed by the United States for twenty-five years to service twenty million dollars in debt, while predicting growing popular resistance against foreign financial dominance across Latin America.
records.summary_es: El *Daily Worker* criticó la misión financiera del exvicepresidente Charles G. Dawes en Santo Domingo, calificándola de estudio imperialista ideado para afianzar nuevos préstamos y un mayor control estadounidense. El artículo remarcó que las aduanas dominicanas habían sido administradas por Estados Unidos durante veinticinco años para solventar una deuda de veinte millones de dólares, al tiempo que vaticinaba una creciente resistencia popular contra la hegemonía financiera extranjera en América Latina.
records.passage: the former vice president, who is himself a big Chicago banker with a shady past, especially in the Lorimer scandal, may simply be conducting a survey to determine what further could profitably be taken under American control as security for another loan. The collection of Dominican customs revenues has already been under the control of the United States government for the past 25 years, to provide interest for the repayment of $20,000,000 rolled up in loans already extended to governments, most of which have been set up by the Wall Street-Washington regime as its pet puppets. After Lindbergh and Hoover, Dawes comes to the West Indies and Latin America to cash in on the "good will" tours of aviators and presidents. The chains of great finance, properly adjusted according to the Dawes method, are expected to make the American semi-colonials easier victims of the Yankee imperialist pickpockets. But there are many indications, as in Santo Domingo at the present time, also Nicaragua, that the workers and peasants of Latin America intend having something to say about this enslaving program of the dollar financial experts. It noted that the dissolution of the Haitian legislature by U.S. Marines had eliminated representative checks on the commissioner's governance.

El artículo sostuvo que Russell toleró la supresión de la libertad de expresión y de la independencia judicial mientras Borno acrecentaba sus prerrogativas ejecutivas. Destacó que la disolución del poder legislativo haitiano a manos de los infantes de marina estadounidenses había eliminado todo contrapeso representativo sobre la gestión del comisionado.
records.passage: What appeared to be a demonstration of Russell's power was given last year when Senator King of Utah, who had criticized American occupation of Haiti, was barred from visiting the country by President Borno. While it could not be shown that Russell had [illegible] inspired the ban, few failed to concede that a word from him to Borno would promptly have averted this affront to an American Senator. With the benign [illegible] tacit approval of Russell, free press and free speech in Haiti have been pretty generally suppressed and Borno has jammed through laws extending his titular dictatorship and effecting his domination of the Haitian courts, which we did not take over under the treaty. American marines long ago dissolved the Haitian congress, so Russell hasn't a representative legislative body to contend with as has our governor general in the Philippines.

records.full_text:
DOMINICAN REBELLION STARTS AS HOOVER COMMISSION DEPARTS

Haiti Commission Sails From Key West; Marines Available to Put Down Any Disorder

Departure of President Hoover's Haitian commission today from Key West coincided with reports of a rebellion in the Dominican Republic which shares the island of Santo Domingo with Haiti.

The U. S. has assumed responsibilities under the existing Dominican-American treaty which might be made the basis for intervention in the Dominican Republic if disorder persists.

President Hoover said today his reports of revolutionary conditions contained no information that there is any danger to the life or liberty of Americans at the present time.

Marines Ready
Marines are available in Haiti and a force could be dispatched to the other part of the island.

Treaty relations between the U. S. and the Dominican Republic are financial. Article I authorizes the President of the U. S. to appoint a General Receiver of Dominican Customs, and Article II says:

“The government of the U. S. will give to the General Receiver and his assistants such protection as it may find to be requisite for the performance of their duties.”

Natives Killed
The President ordered additional marines to Haiti after disorders last December, but subsequently recalled them. Several natives were killed by the marines. The Haitian Commission, headed by Cameron Forbes, former Governor General of the Philippines, is sailing on the U. S. S. Rochester.

Marines were sent to the Dominican republic in 1916 to quiet a serious uprising. They formed a military government which continued in office until 1924 when Rear Admiral Samuel S. Robinson, military governor turned the government over to the newly elected president, Horacio Vasquez, who still is in office.

Extent Unknown
Reports received by the State Department from Minister Charles B. Curtis indicated rebellion against the Vasquez governments and said Senora Vasquez had sought safety in the American Legation. First reports to the department did not define the origin or extent of the disorder.

Dominican affairs have been tranquil for 10 years. The present treaty relationship with the U. S. began in 1907. Between 1865 and 1904 domestic disorder contributed to the creation of a national debt of $32,000,000, much of which was represented by bonds held in European countries.

Roosevelt Acted
In 1905 there were rumors that several European governments contemplated vigorous action in behalf of the bondholders. President Roosevelt negotiated a treaty which was rejected by the Senate because one clause was interpreted as establishing a protectorate.

Roosevelt then negotiated an executive agreement which was put in force, and subsequently put in treaty form.

records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Times* reported that a major rebellion had broken out against Dominican President Horacio Vásquez, prompting his wife to take shelter at the American Legation. Insurgents captured the fort and police station at Santiago de los Caballeros and took control of Dajabón near the Haitian border after disarming local authorities. records.summary_en: The *Daily Worker* reported that Dominican rebels seized Santiago de los Caballeros, Puerto Plata, and La Vega, leading to the resignation of Vice President Alfonseca. The paper charged that President Horacio Vásquez was being kept in power by U.S. Minister Charles B. Curtis and Customs Receiver General William E. Pulliam to protect American financial investments. Curtis reportedly urged Vásquez to reconsider resigning, while the publication denounced the regime as a tool of Wall Street and the National City Bank of New York.

records.summary_en: The *Daily Worker* reported that Dominican President Vásquez offered to repeal electoral amendments extending his term from four to six years as rebel forces over 1,000 strong advanced from the interior. The article stated that public rebellion was fueled by fears that Vásquez would maintain power with U.S. support, alongside severe poverty caused by falling sugar and tobacco prices. It also reported that Vásquez remained in frequent consultation with the American minister regarding marine backing.

El artículo indicó que el descontento popular estuvo avivado por el temor de que Vásquez se perpetuara en el poder con apoyo de Estados Unidos, unido a la extrema miseria provocada por la caída de los precios del azúcar y del tabaco. Reportó además que Vásquez celebraba continuas consultas con el ministro estadounidense en relación con un posible respaldo de la infantería de marina.

records.summary_en: The *Daily Worker* reported that following the marine withdrawal, Dominican President Vásquez assumed dictatorial powers that facilitated American corporate control of over 300,000 acres of sugar plantations. The article cited Charles G. Dawes's 1928 mission to structure the Dominican budget for repayments to the National City Bank under the customs treaty. It further claimed that High Commissioner Russell in Haiti feared the Dominican rebellion would inspire Haitian peasants to revolt against President Borno's administration.

records.summary_en: The *South Bend News-Times* reported that rebel chief Rafael Estrella Ureña entered Santo Domingo to negotiate with President Vásquez and U.S. Minister Charles B. Curtis following the capture of northern and eastern cities by 4,000 insurgent troops. Rebel gunfire around the central plaza and cathedral caused alarm among hotel guests, while government operations ceased. Acting as mediator, Curtis sought a constitutional compromise by appointing a new secretary of the interior who could legally succeed Vásquez.

records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo on September 6 reports that relief agencies reaching the stricken
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo on September 6 reports that relief agencies reaching the stricken city found the horror of Wednesday's hurricane worse rather than better: an estimated 1,500 to 2,000 persons dead, more than 5,000 injured, 30,000 homeless, and of 10,000 buildings only 400 left standing, with property damage to pass $20,000,000. There is no water fit to drink, the dead are being collected and burned in heaps and in concrete cisterns used as funeral pyres, relief planes have brought some supplies and doctors from Port-au-Prince, Havana, the United States and Porto Rico, and the president has stopped food profiteering by ordering all food sold at cost under pain of court martial, while Santiago, La Vega and Puerto Plata are reported undamaged.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Associated Press desde Santo Domingo del 6 de septiembre informa que las agencias de socorro que llegaron a la ciudad devastada encontraron el horror del huracán del miércoles peor en vez de mejor: se estima que murieron entre 1,500 y 2,000 personas, más de 5,000 resultaron heridas, 30,000 quedaron sin hogar y de 10,000 edificios solo 400 quedaron en pie, con daños materiales que pasarán de $20,000,000. No hay agua apta para beber, los muertos están siendo recogidos y quemados en montones y en cisternas de concreto usadas como piras funerarias, aviones de socorro han traído algunos suministros y médicos desde Puerto Príncipe, La Habana, los Estados Unidos y Puerto Rico, y el presidente ha detenido la especulación con los alimentos ordenando que toda la comida se venda al costo bajo pena de consejo de guerra, mientras se informa que Santiago, La Vega y Puerto Plata no sufrieron daños.

records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* reported on catastrophic devastation in Santo Domingo caused by a hurricane that demolished poorer residential districts across a 160-square-mile area. President Rafael Trujillo assumed personal command of military forces to maintain order, clear debris, and organize relief before the arrival of outside assistance. Initial relief ships from Puerto Rico and commercial cable vessels landed medical units and provided emergency tents for 2,000 homeless survivors.
records.summary_es: El *Springfield Weekly Republican* informó sobre la devastación catastrófica en Santo Domingo causada por un huracán que demolió los distritos residenciales más humildes en un área de 160 millas cuadradas. El presidente Rafael Trujillo asumió el mando personal de las fuerzas militares para mantener el orden, despejar escombros y organizar el socorro antes de la llegada de ayuda exterior. Primeros barcos de auxilio procedentes de Puerto Rico y buques de tendido de cable comercial desembarcaron brigadas médicas y proveyeron tiendas de campaña de emergencia para 2 000 damnificados sin hogar.
records.passage: picks strewn over an area of 160 square miles. Tonight it was possible for the first time to drive through any of the streets of the ruined city to gain anything like an intelligent idea of the storm's wreckage. The poorer sections of the city suffered the most damage. Whole areas inhabited by thousands were completely wiped out, without a single house remaining to give shelter. President Rafael Trujillo took heroic measures in his own hands and with troops under his personal command began clearing the streets and roads. He also gave personal attention to maintaining order. Cable Ship Brings Tents When the first relief ships arrived today they found that the efforts of President Trujillo had resulted in shaping conditions so that more headway may be made than had been hoped for. But it will be next week before there are any street lights and it will still be several days before the town water can be turned on. The All-America Cable company's cable ship today brought tents for 2000 persons. Cable Engineer Judo, of the cable ship All-America, who was an eye-witness of the hurricane which hit San Juan, Porto Rico, in September, 1928, declared this afternoon that the destruction wrought by Wednesday's storm was much greater and that the storm's intensity exceeded the San Juan hurricane. records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* reported that emergency relief centers in Santo Domingo were distributing daily food rations to approximately 10,000 hurricane survivors under Red Cross Director Ernest J. records.summary_en: The *Ronan Pioneer* reviewed Latin American political changes in 1930, noting that revolutionary upheavals began in February when Dominican President Horacio Vásquez sought reelection. Vásquez was forced from office after brief skirmishes and succeeded temporarily by General Estrella Ureña. In subsequent elections held on May 16, General Rafael Trujillo was elected president, officially taking office three months later.
records.summary_es: El *Ronan Pioneer* repasó las transformaciones políticas latinoamericanas en 1930, destacando que las conmociones revolucionarias se iniciaron en febrero cuando el presidente dominicano Horacio Vásquez pretendió reelegirse. Vásquez fue forzado a renunciar tras breves escaramuzas y sucedido transitoriamente por el general Estrella Ureña. En los comicios posteriores del 16 de mayo, el general Rafael Trujillo resultó electo presidente, asumiendo oficialmente el cargo tres meses más tarde.
records.passage: virtual dictators were ousted. Four new governments were established. As a preliminary to these events there was a revolution in the Dominican republic in February, the immediate cause being the announced intention of President Horacio Vasquez to stand for re-election. After a few skirmishes Vasquez was forced out of office, [illegible] succeeded temporarily by General Urena. Elections were held on May 16 and Gen. Rafael Trujillo was chosen president and inaugurated three months later. Bolivia was next on the list. There Dr. Hernando Siles tried, like Vasquez, to perpetuate his rule and was driven from office in May by the insurgents. He was permitted to take refuge in Chile, and his much hated right hand man, Gen. Hans Kundt of Prussia, fled back to his German home. A military junta took over the government, its chief being Gen. Carlos Blanco Galindo. Peru followed suit in August. The officers of the army led a movement against President Augusto B. Leguia, who had held the office for more than ten years and considered himself almost irremovable. He was forced to resign, turning over his powers to a military junta, and later Lieut. Col. Luis M. Sanchez Cerro was made provisional president. Leguia had been recognized as an efficient business president and Peru made great material strides during his regime, but the revolutionists accused him of "denial of civil liberties" and also of nepotism and the sale of concessions. He was imprisoned to await trial.

records.summary_en: The *Daily Worker* condemned U.S. support for General Trujillo's regime in the Dominican Republic, noting heavy American capital investments and the use of U.S. currency on the island. Citing declarations from the Caribbean Red Aid, the publication alleged that Dominican authorities arbitrarily arrested workers as vagrants to condemn them to forced labor in brutal prisons. The editorial demanded that U.S. officials apply the same forced-labor import bans to Dominican sugar, cocoa, and tobacco that were imposed against Soviet imports.
records.summary_es: El *Daily Worker* condenó el respaldo estadounidense al régimen del general Trujillo en la República Dominicana, resaltando las cuantiosas inversiones de capital norteamericano y el uso de la moneda de Estados Unidos en la isla. Citando declaraciones del Socorro Rojo del Caribe, el diario denunció que las autoridades dominicanas arrestaban arbitrariamente a trabajadores bajo cargos de vagancia para destinarlos a trabajos forzados en prisiones brutales. El editorial exigió a los funcionarios de Washington aplicar al azúcar, cacao y tabaco dominicanos las mismas restricciones de importación por trabajo forzado impuestas a los productos soviéticos.

Yet what do we hear about forced labor — not in the Soviet Union — but right here at America's doorstep and under its control? The workers' defense organization known as the Caribbean Red Aid, in a recent statement on conditions in Santo Domingo, protests at the terror against the Dominican working class, and says: "The troops stop and question workers in the streets of all the cities of the country and after brief questions and replies declare the passers-by 'vagrants' and take them off under arrest. Each one of those arrested awaits the most terrible prison regime and FORCED LABOR." Perhaps Secretary Mellon of the U. S. Perhaps he will decree that "the burden of proof" rests on the various Yankee imperialist corporations and the National City Bank which finances them, to prove that Dominican sugar, cocoa and tobacco are not produced "in whole or in part by forced labor?" This is the bar put against Soviet lumber this last Monday. Ah, how vigilant the Washington officials are! records.summary_en: The *Douglas Daily Dispatch* reported that Secretary of State Henry L. Stimson contemplated an early withdrawal of U.S. Marines from Haiti, dependent on the efficiency of the local national guard. Stimson stated that Washington aimed to establish a system similar to the Dominican Republic, where security was entrusted to native forces while an American customs receiver managed public revenue. He noted that financial adviser Sidney de la Rue and the guard would safeguard American bondholders.

Stimson declaró que el objetivo de Washington era implantar un sistema similar al de la República Dominicana, donde la seguridad quedaba encomendada a fuerzas nacionales mientras un receptor de aduanas estadounidense administraba los ingresos fiscales. Indicó que el asesor financiero Sidney de la Rue y la guardia protegerían los intereses de los tenedores de bonos estadounidenses.

The secretary said the United States was aiming in general to create a status for Haiti similar to that in the Dominican republic, where the protection was turned over to the national guard with finances still in the hands of an American receiver of customs. records.passage: Haiti in Line of Storms By United Press WASHINGTON, Sept. 11. — The hurricane which swept Porto Rico Thursday night with undetermined damage was reported by the weather bureau today to be approaching Haiti and the Dominican republic with undiminished violence. Dispatches received here said one person was killed and several were injured in San Juan Thursday night. Extent of damage in the interior of Porto Rico was unknown. Meantime, unofficial reports to the Tropical Radio Company said the city of Belize, British Honduras, had been destroyed by a hurricane Thursday night. The reports said 150 persons had been killed. The Belize hurricane was a disturbance far removed from that which hit Porto Rico. The weather bureau believes the former hurricane has about spent its force. It was centered today in the extreme southern part of the Gulf of Mexico. Warnings were sent by the bureau to Belize Thursday night that the city was in danger, but communications were interrupted. The bureau has charted the progress of the Belize disturbance for several days and added to the current hurricanes that one which reached San Juan shortly before midnight. The San Juan disturbance was about half-way between Porto Rico and Haiti today. Estimates of the violence of the hurricane varied from 70 to 100 miles an hour. Wind velocity of the storm which struck Belize was fifty miles an hour when last reported to the weather bureau. United States Consul Taggart was injured slightly. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that the Dominican Republic suspended principal amortization payments on its foreign debt while maintaining interest payments, diverting customs revenues to internal operational expenses. Officials viewed the move as a breach of the 1924 treaty governing the American customs receivership, which required U.S. consent for debt modifications. The article noted that American private investments totaled nearly $70,000,000 alongside over $17,000,000 in Dominican government bonds.

Funcionarios consideraron la medida como una violación del tratado de 1924 que regía la receptoría general de aduanas estadounidense, el cual exigía el consentimiento de Estados Unidos para cualquier modificación de la deuda. El artículo señaló que las inversiones privadas norteamericanas sumaban cerca de 70 000 000 de dólares, además de más de 17 000 000 de dólares en bonos del Estado dominicano.

BATTLE SUCCESSES Nicaraguan Rebel Leader Contributes Article to Honduran Paper. By the Associated Press. TEGUCIGALPA, Honduras, June 15. — Augusto Sandino, Nicaraguan insurgent leader, contributed an article under his own signature to a newspaper here today in which he asserted that in the month of April his men had fought nine battles against the Nicaraguan national guard. Seven United States Marines serving with the guard were killed, he said, and in all the dead numbered 131. Thirty of the guards were wounded and the insurgents captured 29 rifles, seven machine guns and 19,000 cartridges, Sandino wrote. He asserted the only candidate for the Nicaraguan presidency acceptable to him is Gen. Horacio Portocarrero. "Nicaragua will be freed only by the bullets and blood of our people," he wrote, "we will oppose by force of arms whatever election farce may be attempted with the aid of foreign supervision."

records.full_text:
THIS IS NEWS

At least one solvent country has been discovered in these days of unbalanced budgets and record breaking deficits. At Santo Domingo the Treasury of the Dominican Republic has announced that the government of President Trujillo has rigidly maintained its budget during the first six months of 1932, and that payment on foreign and other debts has been promptly met. The administration of this Carribean country is looked upon as a model by our State Department.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported favorably on conditions in the Dominican Republic on the eve of its sixty-ninth national anniversary, noting that President Trujillo's government had strengthened internal order and foreign credit. In contrast to political instability and financial defaults across much of Latin America since 1930, the commentary noted that the Dominican Republic maintained a balanced budget and steady governance. This administrative stability was credited with bolstering public support at home and prestige abroad.

Se atribuyó a esta estabilidad administrativa el haber afianzado el respaldo popular en el país y el prestigio en el extranjero.

This contributes to strengthen the stability of the situation and this stability, in turn, is the best ally of the authorities in coping with the economic needs of the country. The article recounted how Caperton took control of Port-au-Prince, suppressed opposition, and urged troop deployments to secure a financial treaty desired by the State Department and the National City Bank. records.headline: Pan-American Delegates Ready for Conference Opening Today
records.summary_en: One hundred delegates from the American nations gathered in Montevideo for the opening of the Pan-American Conference on economic and peace questions, with the Gran Chaco war between Bolivia and Paraguay and the monetary and debt situations among the subjects expected to be taken up. Cuba's delegation said its program rested on the complete independence of all American countries and freedom from intervention, while Haiti's delegate, Pierre Paul, charged that the United States had for eighteen years supported unjustifiable intervention in Haiti and said he would introduce a resolution establishing the principle of non-intervention. Secretary of State Cordell Hull visited the heads of delegations, including that of the Dominican Republic, and discussed the question of American financial control in Haiti with the Haitian delegation.

La delegación de Cuba declaró que su programa se basaba en la independencia integral de todos los países americanos y en la libertad frente a la intervención, mientras que el delegado de Haití, Pierre Paul, denunció que los Estados Unidos habían sostenido durante dieciocho años una intervención injustificable en Haití y anunció que presentaría una resolución que estableciera el principio de no intervención. The article detailed his measures eliminating government automobiles for legislators and dropping 500 redundant employees from the state payroll. Despite the depression cutting government revenues by more than half, the piece credited Trujillo and his financial adviser with balancing the national budget and maintaining civic order.

A pesar de que la depresión redujo los ingresos fiscales a más de la mitad, la nota atribuyó a Trujillo y a su consejero financiero el haber equilibrado el presupuesto nacional y preservado el orden cívico.

Trujillo began life as a private in the constabulary forces in the island, long operated by the United States Marines; rose to be captain of it, and is now running the country in the thoroughly efficient, if somewhat hard-boiled, fashion of a marine. Trujillo's first act when he took office was to take away from all the members of the Dominican House and Senate their free government automobiles; his next act to drop 500 supernumeraries off the official pay roll. The depression in Santo Domingo cut the state's revenue in half—from $15,000,000 to $7,000,000, and Trujillo found an empty treasury. But now, thanks to Trujillo and to the advice of his financial adviser, the republic has a balanced budget and is sweet, sanitary and safe. Machado was reportedly seeking a new haven in Venezuela under President Gómez.

Según trascendió, Machado buscaba un nuevo asilo en Venezuela bajo el gobierno del presidente Gómez.

records.full_text:
WASHINGTON OBSERVATIONS

The happily concluded negotiations for the adjustment of the foreign dollar bonds of the tiny Dominican Republic as announced last week is a new laurel crown for the Honorable Joseph E. Davies, whose prominent place in the Washington picture dates back to the days of the Wilson administration, when “Joe” Davies was first chairman of the Federal Trade Commission. Now in the private practice of law, though boomed for a place in the Roosevelt cabinet, Mr. Davies numbers the Dominican Republic among his clients and piloted the island’s government through the tortuous channel of debt negotiations with the Foreign Bondholders’ Protective Council. Friends of Mr. Davies are in receipt of copies of his brief in these proceedings, a magnus opus of 200 pages, in which the facts and the law and the argument are skillfully intertwined.

records.summary_en: Former Cuban ruler Gerardo Machado is practically recovered from the attack of indigestion that sent him to a hospital in Santo Domingo two weeks ago and is preparing to sail for Italy. Machado fled Cuba on August 12, 1933, and lived in Canada and the United States while Cuban governments sought his return for trial. His friends denied a version that his illness in Santo Domingo was poisoning, and in the Dominican Republic he was granted refuge by President Rafael Trujillo, long a friend of Machado.

Sus amigos negaron una versión de que su enfermedad en Santo Domingo fue un envenenamiento, y en la República Dominicana recibió refugio del presidente Rafael Trujillo, amigo de Machado desde hacía tiempo.

records.headline: Dominican School System Placed on Modern Basis
records.summary_en: This feature describes the modernization of the Dominican school system under President Trujillo's reconstruction program: in the last year a thousand new rural school buildings have been constructed as part of an intense campaign against illiteracy, built with native materials by the Dominican Party. The program includes a Dominican edition of 20,000 copies of a reading and writing primer by the Catalan educator Eladio Homs, distributed by the President at his own expense to 20,000 rural schoolboys, and a book of the President's own maxims, published for training in citizenship. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published a statement praising President Trujillo for directing the rebuilding of Santo Domingo following its destruction, modernizing the city without incurring new debt or defaulting on bonded interest payments. The report highlighted extensive nationwide public works, including new roads, schools, hospitals, Latin America's largest suspension bridge, and a nearly completed $3,000,000 artificial port at Trujillo City. It added that despite public efforts to rename the capital in his honor, Trujillo had initially opposed the proposal.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* publicó una declaración en la que elogiaba al presidente Trujillo por dirigir la reconstrucción de Santo Domingo tras su destrucción, modernizando la urbe sin contraer nueva deuda ni suspender el pago de intereses sobre los bonos. El informe destacó amplias obras públicas en todo el territorio nacional, como nuevas carreteras, escuelas, hospitales, el puente colgante más grande de América Latina y un puerto artificial de 3.000.000 de dólares a punto de concluirse en Ciudad Trujillo. Añadió que, pese a las gestiones públicas para rebautizar la capital en su honor, Trujillo se había opuesto inicialmente a dicha propuesta.
records.passage: President Trujillo, the statement says: "With a will that brought comment from the entire world, the 39-year-old Chief Executive personally directed the task of saving the impoverished population from starvation and epidemics. and then of constructing a new city to replace the old one. Rapidly new streets, buildings, homes and parks appeared, until Santo Domingo became a new metropolis in gleaming white, far surpassing the city it had replaced. "Without defaulting or postponing Interest payments on bonded indebtedness. and without incurring new indebtedness. President Trujillo conducted a vast program of public works throughout the nation, financed entirely from current revenue. New highways were laid into every corner of the country; great bridges were swung across rivers, among them the largest suspension bridge in Latin America; new schools, hospitals, libraries. were erected everywhere. Agricultural development mounted to new all-time highs and industry leaped from a handful of manufacturing establishments to more than 1,200. After his re-election in 1934. records.headline: With an opening salute of 21 guns from the batteries of Ozama
records.summary_en: With an opening salute of 21 guns from the batteries of Ozama Fortress, the Dominican Republic inaugurated the most extensive and elaborate celebration of Washington's birthday ever held outside the United States. On President Rafael L. Trujillo's suggestion, Congress approved changing the name of Trujillo City's boulevard, until then Avenida Presidente Trujillo, to Avenida George Washington, and the dedication ceremonies included addresses by Trujillo and American Minister Hans F. Arthur Schoenfeld and the unveiling of a large commemorative bronze plaque.
records.summary_es: Con una salva inaugural de 21 cañonazos desde las baterías de la Fortaleza Ozama, la República Dominicana inauguró la celebración más extensa y elaborada del natalicio de Washington jamás realizada fuera de los Estados Unidos. A propuesta del presidente Rafael L. Trujillo, el Congreso aprobó cambiar el nombre del bulevar de Ciudad Trujillo, hasta entonces Avenida Presidente Trujillo, por Avenida George Washington, y las ceremonias de dedicación incluyeron discursos de Trujillo y del ministro estadounidense Hans F. Arthur Schoenfeld y la develación de una gran placa conmemorativa de bronce.
records.passage: holiday. With an opening salute of 21 guns from the batteries of Ozama Fortress, the Dominican Republic today Inaugurated the most extensive and elaborate celebration of Washington's birthday ever held outside the United States. In a gesture of friendship and admiration for the United States and its first President, George Washington, Pres. Gen. Rafael L. Trujillo recently suggested that the name of Trujillo City's most beautiful boulevard, until today called Avenida Presidente Trujillo, be changed to Avenida George Washington. Acting on this suggestion the national congress approved an ordinance to that effect and named February 22, 1936, as the date for the official inaugural ceremonies. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that in accepting President Roosevelt's invitation to a Pan-American conference in Buenos Aires, the Dominican Republic, Colombia, and Guatemala proposed establishing an American league of nations. Dominican President Rafael Trujillo and Colombian President Alfonso López argued that an American league would serve regional purposes more effectively than the League of Nations in Geneva. Guatemala additionally proposed a mutual assistance pact providing for joint action under the Monroe Doctrine against non-American aggression.

El mandatario dominicano Rafael Trujillo y el presidente colombiano Alfonso López sostuvieron que una liga continental respondería mejor a las necesidades de la región que la Sociedad de Naciones en Ginebra. Guatemala propuso además un pacto de asistencia mutua que contemplaba acciones conjuntas al amparo de la Doctrina Monroe frente a agresiones extracontinentales.

As the fitting aftermath of these constructive developments came President Roosevelt's project for an extraordinary conference of Pan-American states to be convened at Buenos Aires this year for the purpose of laying still deeper the foundations of inter-American fraternity. That there is a cordial desire to knit ever more closely the ties of common interest is indicated by the views of Colombia, Guatemala and the Dominican Republic, which propose, while accepting Mr. Roosevelt's invitation, the formation of a league of nations for the Americas. Guatemala also suggests a multilateral pact of mutual assistance, which would provide for joint Pan-American action under the Monroe Doctrine in case of aggression by any non-American power. President Lopez of Colombia and President Trujillo of the Dominican Republic emphasize that a league of American nations would be more efficacious for purely American purposes than the Geneva League. records.summary_en: The *Washington Daily News* reported that Dominican Minister Andrés Pastoriza lodged an unofficial complaint with Assistant Secretary of State Sumner Welles regarding a "March of Time" film depicting President Trujillo. The column commented on the diplomatic challenge Pastoriza faced representing a dictator in the United States while maintaining poise. It also recounted a humorous anecdote about a Cuban sugar expert who became intoxicated on Dominican rum during a picnic on Chesapeake Bay.

La columna comentó el desafío diplomático que enfrentaba Pastoriza al representar a un dictador en Estados Unidos preservando la compostura. records.summary_en: The *Washington Daily News* reported that the Dominican government declared closed the recent frontier incident in which more than 1,000 Haitians were reported killed. Dominican officials asserted that the affair was a private dispute between individuals along the border rather than an international matter, and denied dispatching troops to the frontier. Massacre Stories Assailed as Lies

By LOUIS JAY HEATH
United Press Staff Correspondent

Haitian and Dominican politicians and revolutionists were charged with malicious distortion of a “small incident” which took place early in October near the Dominican-Haitian border, in a formal communique issued by Dominican Minister Andres Pastoriza here today.

Haitian officials have charged that the so-called “small incident” referred to by Pastoriza consisted of “brutal killings of from 3000 to 5000 Haitian nationals by Dominican soldiers and police.” At the request of the Haitian government the United States, Mexico and Cuba have tendered their good offices to mediate the incident. To date the Dominican government has not accepted the tender and has sent special envoys to all three capitols to present the Dominican case.

The Pastoriza communique, addressed to editors, stated that the Dominican government already considered the “incident closed.”

USED BY ENEMIES
“The small incident . . . between Dominican citizens and Haitian citizens who were maintaining illegal residence in certain zones of the Dominican Republic, or who were violently entering the Dominican Republic,” the communique said, “is being used by political enemies of President Trujillo (of the Dominican Republic) and by Haitian elements interested in covering up the political unrest existing for some time in the Republic of Haiti. . . .”

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published an analysis attributing cross-border tensions between Haiti and the Dominican Republic to acute hunger and agricultural underproduction resulting from Haiti's dense population. The writer argued that food shortages drove impoverished Haitians across the frontier to steal livestock and farm animals. In turn, isolated Dominican homesteaders strongly resented these cattle thefts and feared for their lives and families.

El autor sostenía que la escasez de alimentos empujaba a haitianos desposeídos a cruzar la frontera para robar ganado y animales de labranza. Por su parte, los campesinos dominicanos de zonas aisladas resentían profundamente esos robos pecuarios y temían por la integridad de sus familias y vidas.
records.passage: cattle and farm animals. Haiti's teeming population literally cannot subsist on what is produced by their country's backward agriculture. Considerably greater production would be possible in Haiti, despite the fact that the soil has been treated villainously ever since the French were expelled, if it were not for a racial trait which is characteristic of the island. Well does the Haitian peasant know this weakness of his fellow-countrymen. Of what use for him—or, more accurately, for his wife—to work hard and produce an abundance if some one else is to reap the benefit? In Haiti, the prudent peasant never allows fruit to ripen on his trees—if he does, his neighbors, on the first dark night that comes along, will pick it for him. Thus the situation in Haiti is a combination of dense population with underproduction of food. When such a situation comes into being in any country it means trouble—trouble within the country and trouble for the neighbors without. Hunger Basic Cause. In a word, it is hunger, and not just a propensity for vicious thievery, that drives the poverty-stricken Haitians to commit depredations. records.headline: President Vincent asserted that the border question which once existed had
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Haitian President Sténio Vincent estimated 8,000 Haitians were assassinated in the Dominican Republic, maintaining that the border dispute had already been settled by treaty two years prior. Vincent asserted that the Dominican government should have used standard diplomatic channels to repatriate undesirable foreigners, rather than resorting to violence without warning. While Vincent requested mediation from the United States, Cuba, and Mexico, President Trujillo expressed surprise at the appeal, pointing to existing bilateral accords.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el presidente haitiano Sténio Vincent estimó en 8.000 los haitianos asesinados en la República Dominicana, sosteniendo que la disputa de límites ya había quedado resuelta mediante tratado hacía dos años. Vincent aseveró que el gobierno dominicano debió recurrir a los canales diplomáticos habituales para repatriar a los extranjeros indeseables en lugar de acudir a la violencia sin previo aviso. Mientras Vincent solicitaba la mediación de Estados Unidos, Cuba y México, el presidente Trujillo expresó sorpresa ante dicha apelación señalando la vigencia de los acuerdos bilaterales.
records.passage: President Vincent asserted that the border question which once existed had been settled, largely at the initiative of the Haitian government two years ago when a treaty was signed by the two nations. He said there had been no border question since then. Usual Channels Open. "If the Dominican government wanted to expel foreigners they believed for one reason or another undesirable. they could have used the usual channels, the same as Cuba did when it repatriated thousands of Haitians from Cuba recently," President Vincent said. "I vow that this government has never received the slightest indications that Haitians, many of whom resided in the Dominican Republic for many -years, suddenly had become undesirable, until I heard of the assassinations." President Vincent's estimate of 8.000 slain was higher even than reports circulating on the streets of this sultry little mountain capital, where the populace is clamoring for strong measures in dealing with the Dominican Republic. The United States State Department on November 13 announced it had received a request from President Vincent for the United States to offer its good offices, together with Cuba and Mexico, toward seeking a solution of the Haitian-Dominican controversy. When President Rafael Leonidas Trujillo of the Dominican Republic learned of President Vincent's action, he expressed surprise that the United States, Cuba and Mexico had been asked to mediate. He mentioned a diplomatic accord which exists between the two governments.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Dominican Minister Andrés Pastoriza announced President Trujillo would not seek reelection, instead endorsing Dr. Jacinto B. Peynado for president and Dr. Manuel de Jesús Troncoso de la Concha for vice president, though Trujillo remained ready to serve if needed. The announcement came amid ongoing diplomatic friction with Haiti, which alleged that over 12,000 Haitians were massacred on Dominican soil. Dominican officials denied the accusations, attributing the reports to political enemies and citing economic strain caused by illegal Haitian migration.

El anuncio se produjo en medio de continuas fricciones diplomáticas con Haití, que alegaba la masacre de más de 12.000 haitianos en suelo dominicano. Las autoridades dominicanas rechazaron las acusaciones, atribuyendo los informes a enemigos políticos y señalando la carga económica provocada por la inmigración clandestina haitiana.

records.headline: Massacre river and chop sugar cane for wealthier Santo Domingo planters
records.summary_en: The *Times-News* reported that economic hardship and falling sugar prices exacerbated animosity toward thousands of Haitian laborers living in the Dominican Republic, culminating in nocturnal massacres where hundreds of Haitians were butchered with machetes along the Massacre River. Rather than retaliating militarily, Haitian President Sténio Vincent submitted the conflict to the Permanent Committee of Inter-American Conciliation under the 1923 Gondra Treaty. The resulting settlement required the Dominican government to pay a $750,000 indemnity, continue investigating the killings with full publicity, and cooperate to prevent future occurrences.
records.summary_es: El *Times-News* informó que las dificultades económicas y la caída del precio del azúcar avivaron la hostilidad hacia miles de braceros haitianos radicados en la República Dominicana, culminando en matanzas nocturnas donde cientos de haitianos fueron degollados a machetazos a lo largo del río Masacre. En lugar de tomar represalias militares, el presidente haitiano Sténio Vincent sometió la disputa a la Comisión Permanente de Conciliación Interamericana al amparo del Tratado Gondra de 1923. El acuerdo resultante obligó al gobierno dominicano a pagar una indemnización de 750.000 dólares, proseguir las investigaciones judiciales con amplia difusión pública y cooperar para prevenir hechos semejantes en el futuro.

Apparently the solution was found, if peculiarly,; for by night, according to survivors, the Haitians were hauled from their tiny homes and butchered with machetes, butchered by the hundreds, and the bodies left along the banks of Massacre river. When these facts came out of the interior and reached the seaport, foreigners looked at Haiti's president Stenio Vincent for warring retaliation. records.headline: An Adventurers' Club story tells of Charley, who worked six months for a sugar concern at La Romana and, while on vacation
records.summary_en: An Adventurers' Club story tells of Charley, who worked six months for a sugar concern at La Romana and, while on vacation in Santo Domingo City, received orders transferring him to a new project at Barahona, but found every steamer tied up by a steamship strike and no road to take him there. He took a small sailing vessel for what should have been an overnight trip, but a storm blew the boat ten miles off course and disabled its steering gear, leaving him becalmed for days with forty Haitian passengers, no food and hot drinking water, as the only white man aboard, paying the captain ten dollars for protection and sleeping lashed to the rail. On the third night he woke to see two men creeping toward him with machetes in their mouths and shot both dead as the ship erupted in uproar.
records.summary_es: Un relato del Club de Aventureros cuenta la historia de Charley, que trabajó seis meses para una empresa azucarera en La Romana y, estando de vacaciones en la ciudad de Santo Domingo, recibió órdenes de traslado a un nuevo proyecto en Barahona, pero encontró todos los vapores detenidos por una huelga naviera y ningún camino que lo llevara allí. Se embarcó en un pequeño velero para lo que debía ser un viaje de una noche, pero una tormenta desvió el barco diez millas de su rumbo y averió su timón, dejándolo en calma durante días con cuarenta pasajeros haitianos, sin comida y con el agua potable caliente, siendo el único hombre blanco a bordo, pagando al capitán diez dólares por protección y durmiendo atado a la barandilla. En la tercera noche despertó y vio a dos hombres acercándose a él arrastrándose con machetes en la boca, y les disparó a ambos hasta matarlos mientras el barco estallaba en alboroto.
records.passage: was hot and humid. Hunger gnawed at his innards, but he had to make the best of it. The natives were getting more and more restless. They eyed Charley's clothes with covetous looks that became more and more insolent and apparent. And still there was no sign of the wind that would blow them into Barahona. That night, worn out by two days and nights of wakefulness, Charley fell asleep. Sometime in the dark hours he woke up suddenly, by sheer instinct. In the dim light of a tropic moon he saw two dark figures creeping along the deck toward him — two natives — great, husky blacks with machetes in their mouths! "They didn't know my eyes were open," he says, "if they had known it I wouldn't be alive today. But their ignorance gave me an opportunity to draw my guns." Charley got those guns out just as the natives were taking their machetes from their mouths. He whipped up one gun and fired twice. In an instant, two men were dead on the deck and the whole ship was in an uproar. Dark figures came swarming toward him. The captain was a big, powerful fellow. Charley says he was built on the style of Harry Wills in his prime. He picked Charley up with one hand, threw him into his cabin head first, and then, with the aid of a revolver and his powerful physique, held that furious mob at bay. Captain Threatens to Sink the Ship. The next morning the captain held an inquiry, announced that Charley had shot in self-defense, and threatened to sink the ship if any more attempts were made on his life. "Calm was restored

records.summary_en: The *Washington Times* reported that thirty-two German-Jewish refugees arriving in New York aboard the Red Star liner *Westernland* planned to establish new homes in the Dominican Republic. The article noted that the country's capital, originally named Santo Domingo, had been renamed Ciudad Trujillo by Rafael Trujillo, whose past record with immigrants was criticized. The arrival occurred as over 1,500 Jewish refugees faced potential return to Germany after Paraguay and Uruguay barred their entry.

El artículo anotó que la capital del país, originalmente llamada Santo Domingo, había sido rebautizada Ciudad Trujillo por Rafael Trujillo, cuyos antecedentes hacia la inmigración eran objeto de críticas. Su llegada se produjo mientras más de 1.500 refugiados judíos se enfrentaban a una posible repatriación a Alemania tras prohibírseles la entrada en Paraguay y Uruguay.

Passport visas granted at later dates to the refugees now on their way to South America were said to be fraudulent. records.summary_en: The *Washington Daily News* commented on reports that General Rafael Trujillo and his entourage were traveling to Germany, raising speculation about German interest in Samaná Bay as a potential submarine base. Although the Dominican Legation denied that Trujillo would meet Adolf Hitler, it did not deny he was traveling to Germany. The report also listed members of Señora de Trujillo's party, which included military aides, a private physician, and secretary J. M. Bonetti Burgos.
records.summary_es: El *Washington Daily News* comentó los informes de que el general Rafael Trujillo y su comitiva viajaban a Alemania, lo que suscitó conjeturas en torno al interés germano en la bahía de Samaná como posible base submarina. Pese a que la Legación dominicana desmintió que Trujillo fuera a entrevistarse con Adolf Hitler, no negó que viajara a territorio alemán. La crónica enumeró asimismo a los miembros de la comitiva de la señora de Trujillo, en la que figuraban edecanes militares, un médico de cabecera y el secretario J. M. Bonetti Burgos.

Some time ago, the Dominican Legation went to great pains to announce that Gen. Trujillo "was not going to visit Hitler." In denying the report that the generalissimo would not pay a visit to Der Fuehrer, there was no denial that he was not going to Germany! And why shouldn't he go to see Hitler? No reason except perhaps it would be better if the Reichschancellor didn't wind up a deal on that same Samana Bay of which we spoke the other day. President Roosevelt didn't do any negotiating for the use of Samana Bay as a marine base when he was in southern waters. At least we haven't heard that he did. But Herr Hitler has long thought Samana Bay would be an excellent submarine base for himself! LENGTHY VISIT HERE? Last autumn, when Gen. records.headline: This column reports rumours that General Trujillo himself is aboard the Santa Paula with his family's party, which
records.summary_en: This column reports rumours that General Trujillo himself is aboard the Santa Paula with his family's party, which travelled incognito and embarked at Cape Haitien, and that Dominican Minister Andres Pastoriza and consular officials will meet the ship at Quarantine, with Mayor LaGuardia to welcome the party to a floor of the Waldorf in New York. It passes on speculation that the party is en route to Germany, noting that the Dominican Legation had denied only that Trujillo would visit Hitler, and that Hitler has long thought Samana Bay would make an excellent submarine base.
records.summary_es: Esta columna recoge los rumores de que el propio general Trujillo viaja a bordo del Santa Paula con el grupo de su familia, que viajó de incógnito y embarcó en Cabo Haitiano, y de que el ministro dominicano Andrés Pastoriza y funcionarios consulares recibirán el barco en la cuarentena, con el alcalde LaGuardia para dar la bienvenida al grupo a un piso del Waldorf en Nueva York. Se hace eco de la especulación de que el grupo va rumbo a Alemania, señalando que la legación dominicana solo había negado que Trujillo visitaría a Hitler, y que Hitler ha pensado durante mucho tiempo que la bahía de Samaná sería una excelente base de submarinos.

He did not look like an artist. And he certainly did not look like the greatest artist of them all. He was a big, clumsy man whose heavy, spatulate hands appeared more adapted to grasping a shovel than a camel's hair brush. His eyes alone were a clue to his eminence; keen gray eyes which seemed to be able to survey the world — and more. Those gray eyes were narrowed as they turned first to the young man and then lingered on the girl seated opposite him. They were nervous, those two. The young man plucked at the frayed edge of his cuff. His sensitive mouth twitched spasmodically. The girl was tense. Her finely molded face was unnaturally pale. She drew up the collar of her shabby coat as tho she were suddenly cold. Finally, the great man spoke. "It has been hard going, I understand." He smiled sympathetically. records.summary_en: The writer dismisses a report, emanating from Puerto Rico, where a number of exiled enemies of General Trujillo live, that Trujillo had negotiated with Germany to lease Samaná Bay as a submarine base. Leasing the bay to the Nazis would be a hostile act toward the United States, the piece argues, and in any emergency Trujillo would instead permit the United States Navy to use Samaná Bay or any other Dominican port.

Arrendar la bahía a los nazis sería un acto hostil hacia los Estados Unidos, sostiene el texto, y en cualquier emergencia Trujillo permitiría más bien que la Armada estadounidense usara la bahía de Samaná o cualquier otro puerto dominicano.

Trujillo had negotiated with Germany for the lease of that strategic body of water as a submarine base. The report emanated from Puerto Rico, where there are a number of exiled enemies of the Generalissimo. It does seem that in view of the fact the General desires only the friendliest relations with this country, he would be smarter than to enter into any such negotiations. Especially when he had so recently entertained a number of prominent Americans in his own house. The lease of the bay to the Nazis would not only be an unfriendly act to the United States, but a hostile one. And, also in view of this same friendliness, it is certain that at any emergency the General would permit the United States Navy the use of Samana Bay or any other Dominican port, as a submarine base or any other military faculty. records.headline: As a former member of the United States Marine Corps—during the
records.summary_en: The *Washington Daily News* outlined the itinerary for General Rafael Trujillo's visit to Washington, D.C., following an invitation from Marine Corps Commandant Major General Thomas Holcomb. The schedule included wreath-laying ceremonies at Mount Vernon and Arlington National Cemetery, official meetings with Secretary of State Cordell Hull and President Roosevelt, and a Senate luncheon. Trujillo was also scheduled to inspect military sites including the Navy Yard, Marine Barracks, and Fort Meade.
records.summary_es: El *Washington Daily News* detalló el itinerario de la visita del general Rafael Trujillo a Washington D.C., tras una invitación cursada por el comandante del Cuerpo de Infantería de Marina, mayor general Thomas Holcomb. El programa incluía ofrendas florales en Mount Vernon y en el Cementerio Nacional de Arlington, reuniones oficiales con el secretario de Estado Cordell Hull y el presidente Roosevelt, así como un almuerzo en el Senado. Se tenía previsto además que Trujillo inspeccionara instalaciones castrenses como el Astillero Naval, el Cuartel de Marines y Fort Meade.

records.headline: The paper sets out the Washington program for former President Rafael L. Trujillo
records.summary_en: The paper sets out the Washington program for former President Rafael L. Trujillo, now commander in chief of the Dominican army, who arrives Thursday: luncheon at the Senate on Friday, visits that afternoon to the Navy Yard and the Marine Barracks, and dinner that night as honor guest of Marine Corps Commandant Thomas Holcomb. On Saturday he will visit Fort Meade, lunch at the Army Navy Club and attend a reception at the Pan-American Union, on Sunday the Haitian Minister, Elie Lescot, will give a luncheon in his honor, and on Monday he will review troops at Quantico and attend a dinner by Chief of Staff George C. Marshall before leaving the capital Tuesday.

El sábado visitará Fort Meade, almorzará en el Army Navy Club y asistirá a una recepción en la Unión Panamericana, el domingo el ministro haitiano, Elie Lescot, ofrecerá un almuerzo en su honor, y el lunes pasará revista a las tropas en Quantico y asistirá a una cena del jefe de Estado Mayor, George C. Marshall, antes de salir de la capital el martes.

records.headline: Even if he is denounced as a tyrant and accused of
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* profiled General Rafael Trujillo, noting that despite being denounced as a tyrant and accused of the massacre of thousands of Haitians two years earlier, he was recognized for administrative energy and public works. Having taken power in 1930 under the slogan "God and Trujillo," he oversaw road construction, school expansion, and the rebuilding and renaming of the capital before handing the presidency to Dr. Jacinto Bienvenido Peynado. The article noted that Trujillo continued to direct Dominican governance while being celebrated by sympathetic biographers as an inspired leader.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* perfiló al general Rafael Trujillo, señalando que, a pesar de haber sido denunciado como un tirano y acusado de la matanza de miles de haitianos dos años antes, se le reconocía por su empuje administrativo y sus planes de obras públicas. Habiendo tomado el poder en 1930 bajo el lema «Dios y Trujillo», dirigió la construcción de caminos, la expansión de escuelas y la reedificación y cambio de nombre de la capital antes de traspasar la presidencia formalmente al Dr. Jacinto Bienvenido Peynado. El artículo consignaba que Trujillo seguía conduciendo las riendas del gobierno dominicano mientras biógrafos afines lo ensalzaban como un líder providencial.

Even if he is denounced as a tyrant and accused of the massacre of thousands of Haitians two years ago, during a border struggle along the boundary between the Dominican Republic and Haiti, there is no doubt that he is a forceful leader with a certain genius in public finance. He has an extraordinary concept of himself as a child of destiny When he was still a boy, he resolved to be the president of the Dominican Republic, where storm and strife in politics and insecurity of tenure for presidents was the classical political situation. He won the post in 1930, when he was 39, after a campaign whose slogan was "God and Trujillo." He relinquished it last August to a devoted follower. Dr. Jacinto Bienvenido [Peynado?], who still follows his wishes devotedly. Gen. Trujillo's biographer suggests that in his governing he is guided by an "electric force" from Heaven. He has built roads and pursued other public works, increased the number of public schools, reconstructed the ancient capital of the republic, Santo Domingo, after the 1930 hurricane (and renamed it in his own honor) and enhanced the lot of those persons in his country who are willing to accept his leadership. He is energetic, industrious and a born leader. An inspired biography of him published as a panegyric is revealing for all its encomiums. Progress Through Discipline. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that General Rafael Trujillo hosted a lavish reception at the New York World's Fair aboard his yacht *Ramfis*, formerly owned by American millionaire Julius Fleischmann, before the vessel steamed toward Washington. The article noted Trujillo's fondness for military attire and listed dozens of high foreign orders and medals bestowed upon him across Europe and the Americas. Observers commented that Trujillo possessed more decorations than nearly any other anticipated foreign visitor.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el general Rafael Trujillo ofreció una suntuosa recepción en la Feria Mundial de Nueva York a bordo de su yate *Ramfis*, perteneciente con anterioridad al magnate estadounidense Julius Fleischmann, antes de que el buque zarpase hacia Washington. La nota hizo hincapié en la predilección de Trujillo por las galas militares y enumeró decenas de condecoraciones y medallas extranjeras que le habían sido otorgadas en Europa y América. Los observadores comentaron que Trujillo ostentaba más preseas que casi cualquier otro visitante distinguido del exterior.

The general went from Dominica to Miami aboard the yacht, and it is steaming now up the Atlantic Coast to Washington, where it will be docked when it comes time for the visitor to depart. The general is a man who likes gold braid, and even though he gave up the Dominican presidency last August, he still cuts a dashing sartorial figure. Royal personages excepted, he has more decorations than any visitor expected in Washington this year. Among them are From Italy, Knight Commander of the Crown of Italy; from Spain. records.summary_en: At a brief Washington press conference, General Trujillo, flanked by Minister Pastoriza and Señor Aguilar, described his trip as a goodwill visit to improve relations between the Dominican Republic and the United States before going to the State Department. He said he intended to spend July in the United States inquiring into its agriculture, industry and cultural centers, and that he had received no overtures from the German government.

Dijo que pensaba pasar julio en Estados Unidos investigando su agricultura, industria y centros culturales, y que no había recibido propuestas del gobierno alemán.
