records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that the Dominican Chamber of Commerce in the United States defended General Rafael Trujillo against criticism from the Committee for Dominican Democracy regarding his White House visit with President Roosevelt. The chamber praised Trujillo's public welfare and development achievements in the Dominican Republic. Meanwhile, Trujillo visited troops at Fort George G. Meade, while a reception scheduled at the Pan American Union was canceled out of respect for the late Secretary of the Navy Claude A. Swanson.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que la Cámara de Comercio Dominicana en Estados Unidos salió en defensa del general Rafael Trujillo ante los cuestionamientos formulados por el Committee for Dominican Democracy con motivo de su visita a la Casa Blanca para reunirse con el presidente Roosevelt. Dicha corporación comercial ensalzó las obras de bienestar social y de fomento material alcanzadas por Trujillo en la República Dominicana. Entretanto, Trujillo visitó a las tropas en Fort George G. Meade, al tiempo que una recepción programada en la Unión Panamericana fue cancelada en señal de duelo por el fenecido secretario de Marina Claude A. Swanson.

"As Americans, we strongly resent any criticism of the President of the United States from such a source, insulting his distinguished guest." the chamber declared in a statement for the press. It added: "We members of the Dominican Chamber of Commerce in the United States, composed of American business men, know that the accomplishments achieved by Gen. Trujillo during his administration have far exceeded any public welfare program ever instituted in his country." The general, who will be here until Tuesday, when he departs by yacht for New York, went to Fort George G. Meade. Md., today to see the troops there. A reception at the Pan American Union which had been planned for tonight in the general's honor by Minister Pastoriza of the Dominican Republic has been canceled out of respect to the late Secretary Swanson. records.headline: Fish is quoted as having said at a dinner to Trujillo
records.summary_en: Columnist Raymond Clapper in the *Washington Daily News* criticized Representative Hamilton Fish for praising General Trujillo's regime as a "golden age" during a New York dinner. Clapper cited first-hand reporting by Quentin Reynolds of *Collier's*, who investigated the border atrocities and observed victims mutilated by Dominican forces. Clapper maintained that any prosperity Trujillo claimed was purchased through the murder of thousands of obscure Haitian peasants.

Clapper aseveró que cualquier prosperidad exhibida por Trujillo se pagó con la sangre y el exterminio de miles de humildes campesinos haitianos.

records.summary_en: A society column describes an informal cocktail party at the Dominican legation in Washington, with handwritten invitations reading 'In honor of Gen. records.summary_en: The *Gazette* contrasted the lavish military honors previously accorded to Latin American dictators like Trujillo with the restrained, informal reception given to visiting Haitian President Sténio Vincent in Washington. Despite Vincent being the sitting president of a nation of 2.6 million, he received no 21-gun salute, fanfare, or military parade, meeting only Undersecretary of State Sumner Welles and a small delegation at the station. Critics questioned the appropriateness of celebrating authoritarian figures while giving a chilly welcome to the head of a neighboring constitutional republic.

records.full_text:
Dominicans to Admit
100,000 Refugees

By the Associated Press.

CIUDAD TRUJILLO, Jan. 31.—A contract signed here between the Dominican government and the Dominican Republic Settlement Association provides for the immediate admisison of some 500 European political refugee families and aims at the establishment of 100,000 refugees over a period of years.

Most of the first group are German Jewish refugees, but the contract does not specify nationalities.

The settlement association will pay for establishing them and is to be reimbursed by income from their lands once they have regained their financial feet.

records.headline: Dominican Republic Boss Bans Discussion of War
records.summary_en: NEA correspondent Thomas J. B. Wenner reports from Ciudad Trujillo that members of the Dominican Republic's only legal political party have been ordered not to discuss the European war, a decree of Generalissimo Rafael Leonidas Trujillo Molina, the country's virtual dictator. Party director Paino Pichardo explained that Trujillo, an ardent advocate of Pan-Americanism and a friend of the United States, does not wish his work to be made more difficult by sentiments at variance with the country's declared policy, and insisted the agreement applies to party members, not to the population at large. The article profiles Trujillo, 49, president since 1930, whose name the capital bears, and describes the armed forces he has modernized: a standing army of about 4,000 men, a navy of one military transport and several coast guard vessels, and an air force of about 25 planes.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that the State Department agreed to terminate the U.S. customs receivership in the Dominican Republic, restoring duty collections of roughly $4,000,000 annually to Dominican authorities. In exchange, the Dominican Republic granted the United States a first lien on its total revenues, estimated at $12,000,000, to guarantee the servicing of $15,400,000 in external debt. The treaty was negotiated in Ciudad Trujillo by U.S. Ambassador Hugh Wilson and Dominican Foreign Minister Arturo Despradel, ending the 1924 convention.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el Departamento de Estado acordó extinguir la receptoría aduanera estadounidense en la República Dominicana, devolviendo a las autoridades dominicanas la recaudación de tributos, estimada en unos 4.000.000 de dólares anuales. Como contraparte, la República Dominicana concedió a Estados Unidos un gravamen preferente sobre la totalidad de sus rentas fiscales, calculadas en 12.000.000 de dólares, para afianzar el servicio de 15.400.000 dólares de deuda externa. El tratado fue pactado en Ciudad Trujillo por el embajador estadounidense Hugh Wilson y el canciller dominicano Arturo Despradel, poniendo término a la convención de 1924.
records.passage: Terminated by U. S. By the Associated Press. The State Department announced yesterday that the United States had agreed to terminate its receivership of the Dominican Republic customs revenues and restore to that nation the privilege of handling collection of the approximately $4,000,000 annual intake from duties. In turn, the Dominican government agreed to give the United States first lien on total revenues of the Dominican government, a figure roughly estimated at $12,000.000. The department announced that the agreement was reached in Ciudad Trujillo by a United States commission headed by Ambassador Hugh Wilson and a Dominican commission headed by Arturo Despradel, Minister of Foreign Affairs. The agreement, embodied in a convention, terminates the convention of 1934 by which the United States assumed general receivership of customs in order to guarantee the servicing of the Dominican Republic's external debt of 1922 and 1928, computed at $15,400,000. records.summary_en: The *Daily Alaska Empire* reported that several New York creditors, including Louis Sherry, Cartier, Annin Flag Company, and an art gallery, sought payment from General Rafael Trujillo for services and goods provided during the previous year's World's Fair reception. Although creditors hired a lawyer and dispatched a U.S. Marshal to his hotel, Trujillo was shielded from legal action because he held diplomatic immunity as an Ambassador Extraordinary. As a result, creditors were unable to collect the debts or seize his yacht *Ramfis*, docked at the Washington Navy Yard.

Si bien los acreedores contrataron a un letrado y comisionaron a un alguacil federal (U.S. Marshal) a su hotel, Trujillo quedó a salvo de acciones judiciales en virtud de su inmunidad diplomática como embajador extraordinario. Por consiguiente, los demandantes no pudieron cobrar los créditos ni embargar su yate *Ramfis*, atracado en el Astillero Naval de Washington.

records.summary_en: In the *Washington Daily News*, columnist Ludwell Denny discussed executive war powers and unilateral presidential foreign actions without congressional approval. Denny cited historical precedents where American presidents ruled foreign territories directly or through puppets, specifically referencing past interventions in Haiti, the Dominican Republic, and Nicaragua.
records.summary_es: En *The Washington Daily News*, el columnista Ludwell Denny analizó las facultades bélicas del Poder Ejecutivo y las decisiones unilaterales de política exterior tomadas por presidentes estadounidenses sin aprobación legislativa. Denny trajo a colación precedentes históricos en que mandatarios norteamericanos gobernaron comarcas foráneas directamente o valiéndose de gobernantes títeres, aludiendo puntualmente a las intervenciones militares pasadas en Haití, la República Dominicana y Nicaragua.

records.headline: Wilson recently negotiated a new customs treaty with the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Secretary of State Cordell Hull commended diplomat Hugh R. Wilson for completing confidential assignments, which included negotiating a new customs treaty with the Dominican Republic. The treaty was understood to be ready for submission to the U.S. Senate for ratification. Wilson had previously served as Ambassador to Germany and held various diplomatic posts before focusing on wartime issues in Europe and Latin America.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el secretario de Estado Cordell Hull felicitó al diplomático Hugh R. Wilson por la culminación de misiones reservadas, entre las cuales figuró la negociación de un nuevo tratado de aduanas con la República Dominicana. Se daba por hecho que el instrumento internacional estaba listo para ser sometido al Senado de EE. UU. para su debida ratificación. Wilson se había desempeñado previamente como embajador en Alemania y ocupado diversos cargos diplomáticos antes de volcarse a asuntos bélicos en Europa y América Latina.
records.passage: Hull praising Mr. Wilson's services and saying "certain important and confidential work" which he had undertaken "has now been satisfactorily completed." Mr. Hull's letter did not indicate the nature of the work to which he referred. Mr. Wilson recently negotiated a new customs treaty with the Dominican Republic which is understood now to be ready for submission to the Senate for ratification. His work at the State Department also has been concerned with special problems arising from the war in Europe. Mr. Wilson, who is 55 years old. entered the foreign service in 1911 and has held posts in Lisbon, Guatemala. Buenos Aires, Vienna. Berne and Tokio, as well as Berlin. He also served as chief of the Division of Current Information and as an Assistant Secretary at the State Department. As a protest against Nazi anti-Semitic and other policies, Mr. Wilson was called home from Berlin "for report and consultation" in November, 1938. The German Ambassador was recalled to Berlin soon thereafter. There has been no indication that a new Ambassador to Germany would be appointed. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that diplomatic representatives across the Americas accepted invitations to the Pan-American Aviation Day ball at the Mayflower Hotel. A special invitation was extended to General Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic, who was staying in New York. The event featured decorations provided by Latin American embassies and participation from Cuban aviators.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que representantes del cuerpo diplomático de las Américas acogieron las invitaciones al baile del Día de la Aviación Panamericana en el Mayflower Hotel. Se cursó una invitación de honor al general Rafael Trujillo, de la República Dominicana, quien residía temporalmente en Nueva York. La velada contó con ornamentaciones suministradas por embajadas hispanoamericanas y con la presencia de aviadores cubanos.
records.passage: Senor Dr. Gabriel Turbay and the Minister of Costa Rica and Senora de Fernandez are among the latest Pan-American diplomats to accept invitations to the Pan-American Aviation Day ball, to be held tomorrow night at the Mayflower Hotel. A special invitation has been sent to Gen. Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic. Gen. Trujillo is now in New York. Members of the "Escuadrilla de Aviacion Interamericana de Cuba" also have been invited. This group is scheduled to take part in the Havana celebration of Pan-American Aviation Day and the plan is to have them fly here in time to be honor guests at the Washington celebration. Embassies and Legations of the Latin American republics are to supply decorations emblematic of their countries for use at the celebration here. A general Pan-American motif of decoration will be used. Manor House Unit Of D. A. R. to Meet Tuesday Night Manor House Chapter. Daughters of the American Revolution, will hold its December meeting in the historic Stephen Boomer Balsh house in Georgetown tomorrow at 8:30 p.m. The house, which is now the home of Miss Helen Montgomery, has been marked by the D. A. R. A skit, re-enacting a Christmas Eve in 1830, will be presented, following a business meeting. Dr. Clifton P. Clark will impersonate the Rev. Mr. Balsh. A mitten shower for one of the D. A. R. schools also will be a feature. Honor guests will include Mrs. Charles Carroll Haig. Mrs. Harry C. Oberholser and Mrs. Geoffrey Creyke. Miss Minne Hunt is the chapter regent.

records.headline: The April meeting of Sorosis was held Tuesday evening
records.summary_en: The April meeting of Sorosis, a women's club in Chadbourn, was held on Tuesday evening with Mrs. B. W. Peal as hostess, and a dinner was served to the members on their arrival. During the business meeting, twenty-five new books for the children's shelf of the town library were put on display. Concluding the year's study of Latin America, Mrs. T. O. Goodman presented the countries of Puerto Rico, Haiti and the Dominican Republic.

records.summary_en: The *West Virginia Digest* profiled newly elected Haitian President Élie Lescot, outlining his earlier service as Haiti's Envoy Extraordinary and Minister Plenipotentiary to Ciudad Trujillo. In that post, Lescot helped negotiate the settlement of the border dispute between Haiti and the Dominican Republic, earning the Dominican decoration of Juan Pablo Duarte. He subsequently served as a delegate to the Buenos Aires peace conference before becoming Haitian Minister to the United States in 1937.
records.summary_es: El *West Virginia Digest* perfiló la biografía del recién electo mandatario haitiano Élie Lescot, reseñando su desempeño diplomático anterior como enviado extraordinario y ministro plenipotenciario de Haití en Ciudad Trujillo. En aquella misión, Lescot facilitó las gestiones conciliatorias del pleito limítrofe entre Haití y la República Dominicana, lo que le valió la condecoración dominicana de la Orden de Juan Pablo Duarte. Con posterioridad asistió como delegado a la conferencia de paz de Buenos Aires antes de asumir como ministro plenipotenciario de Haití ante los Estados Unidos en 1937.
records.passage: the early age of twenty-seven he was elected to Legislative Assembly where he served with distinction for three years. At the close of this experience he entered the judiciary finally winning promotion to the cabinet portfolio of Secretary of Public Education and Agriculture in the administration of President Borno. President Vincent made him Secretary of Justice and of the Interior and later sent him to Ciudad Trujillo, the Dominican Republic, as Envoy Extraordinary and Minister Plenipotentiary of the Haitian government. He settled the vexing boundary dispute between Haiti and Santo Domingo, receiving from the Dominican government the cross of the "Gran Oficial del Orden de Merito de Juan Pablo Duarte." President Vincent bestowed upon him the title of "Grand officier de l'Ordre Honneur et Merite" for achievements as Secretary of the Interior. He also was among the Haitian delegates to the Inter-American Conference for the Maintenance of Peace at Buenos Aires. In April, 1937, M. Lescot presented his credentials to President F. D. Roosevelt, as Haitian minister to the United States, succeeding M. [Albert?] Blanchet. His activities in the United States have been unprecedented in promoting and cementing better economic relations between his country and the United States as well as increasing the exchange of cultural amenities, and a practical program of exchange of college students for the purpose of a reciprocal assimilation of language and customs. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* assessed the military vulnerabilities of Hispaniola, noting that the island's extensive coastline could offer bases to enemy forces threatening U.S. naval installations at Guantanamo Bay and Puerto Rico. While the Dominican Republic possessed a larger army than Haiti, it lacked airplanes, anti-aircraft weaponry, and artillery capable of resisting naval or aerial invasion. The article highlighted substantial pro-Axis sentiment in Santo Domingo, with British diplomats estimating that 75 percent of the populace favored Germany, though American observers believed sympathies were evenly divided.

UU. en Guantánamo y Puerto Rico. Aunque la República Dominicana contaba con un ejército más numeroso que Haití, adolecía de aviación bélica, cañones antiaéreos y artillería costera para repeler incursiones navales o bombardeos aéreos. El reportaje puso de relieve un arraigado sentir favorable al Eje en Santo Domingo, calculando los diplomáticos británicos que un 75 por ciento simpatizaba con Alemania, mientras que observadores estadounidenses estimaban dividida la opinión pública.

records.full_text:
Delegates Arriving
For Inter-American
Economic Parley

Welles to Be Keynoter
At Conference Here
Opening Tuesday

By HAROLD B. ROGERS.

As distinguished delegations of finance ministers, heads of central banks, and technical experts from the other American republics continued to arrive over the week-end, plans were being put into final shape for the first Inter-American Conference on Systems of Economic and Financial Control, to open Tuesday at the Pan American Union.

Under the agenda for the conference, which was authorized by the January meeting of Foreign Affairs Ministers at Rio de Janeiro, two different committees will be set up among the delegates. One will consider “international transactions” the other “domestic transactions,” as protection against Axis influence.

The first and last sessions of the conference will be public meetings, but the intervening technical sessions, under present plans probably will be behind closed doors, unless other public sessions “are agreed upon and so ordered by the delegates.” The conference may last about 10 days.

Republics Each Have One Vote.

Each of the 21 republics will have but one vote, regardless of the size of their various delegations.

“Proposals, reports, and projects,” it is provided in the agenda, “shall be considered approved when they have obtained the affirmative vote of an absolute majority of the countries represented at the respective meeting.”

The conference is only one of the several new inter-American developments which have grown out of the second World War to help the American republics present a more united front to the aggressor nations of Germany, Japan and Italy.

Authorized specifically by the Rio Conference of Foreign Ministers, this new gathering is operating under sponsorship of the Inter-American Financial and Economic Advisory Committee. This committee was set up in 1939 and has been regularly functioning since the outbreak of the second World War. At its headquarters in the Pan American Union, this committee, headed by Undersecretary of State Welles, has been holding regularly scheduled meetings and has prepared a comprehensive background of data, which according to experts, should provide much material of value for the forthcoming meeting.

Welles to Be “Keynoter.”

Mr. Welles, who will deliver the opening “keynote” address to the conference, and Dr. Leo S. Rowe, director general of the Pan American Union, who will welcome the delegates, will be followed by a spokesman for the Latin American group. This spokesman will be selected at a preliminary meeting of the delegates tomorrow. There was no official indication today as to who this spokesman may be.

Problems to be considered by the conference, involving the severance of commercial and financial ties between the Western Hemisphere and the Axis powers, are considered by officials to be virtually parallel to the vital issues of breaking diplomatic relations with the Axis, which absorbed major public attention at the Rio conference.

By the terms of two financial and economic resolutions at Rio, it was explained last night by one official, economic intercourse between the American republics and the Axis powers is to be cut; and transactions by nationals of Axis states, likely to benefit members of the tripartite pact (Germany, Italy and Japan) are to be placed under rigid control and supervision.

Other inter-American measures have been adopted to meet economic problems arising out of the war. The Inter-American Development Commission has set up national commissions in each of the Latin-American countries and is especially interested in the development of new industries in each country for which there may be markets in the other republics.

Commission’s Duties.

The Inter-American Maritime Technical Commission, created only a few months ago, is designed primarily to supervise the operation of the immobilized vessels taken over in ports of the American republics. The Office of Co-ordinator of Inter-American Affairs and the Board of Economic Warfare have wide authority and operate extensively in Latin-American affairs.

Over all the American representatives in these agencies, the State Department has exercised a guiding hand, though allowing to some far-reaching autonomy, within the limits of the general international policies laid down by the administration. The Inter-American Defense Board recommends defense measures.

The new program of international solidarity in the economic sphere aimed at by the Rio conference, according to Dr. Rowe, “was nothing short of pooling the resources of the American continent for the winning of the war, and at the same time adopting measures to protect the economic and financial structure of all the republics. The motive that guided the (Rio) delegates,” he added, “was not the selfish interest of any individual state, but the safety and welfare of the entire Western World.”

Many foreign delegations already have arrived and established headquarters. Some are in hotels, others are understood to be established in connection with their embarries or legations. Some of the delegates are ambassadors or ministers.

Brazilian Group Arrives.

Among the first to arrive recently was the group from Brazil. This delegation is headed by Francisco Alves dos Santos, jr., director of exchange, Bank of Brazil. With his technical adviser, Achilles Moreaux of the Bank of Brazil, and other experts he is at the Shoreham Hotel.

Delegates from the other republics, according to the official list, are as follows: Argentina, Eduardo Gagneaux, assistant general manager, Central Bank of Argentina; Bolivia, Humberto Cuenca, general manager, Central Bank of Bolivia; Chile, Pedro Enrique Alfonso, former Minister of Finance; Colombia, Alberto Bayon, chief, Office of Exchange and Import Control; Costa Rica, Paul Gurdian, former Minister of Foreign Affairs and former Minister of Finance; Cuba, Ramiro Guerra Sanchez, representative of Cuba on the Inter-American Financial and Economic Advisory Committee; Dominican Republic, Harry E. Henneman, speci[illegible] representative of the Ministry of Finance and Commerce; Ecuador, Eduardo Icaza, president, Central Bank; El Salvador, Carlos Adalberto Alfaro, charge d’affairs of El Salvador here; Guatemala, Luis Beltranena, dean, School of Economic Scieinces, University of Guatemala; Haiti, Abel La Croix, Minister of Finance; Honduras, Julian R. Caceres, Minister of Honduras here; Mexico, Eduardo Villaseñor, director, Bank of Mexico; Nicaragua, Leon De Bayle, Minister of Nicaragua here; Panama, Ricardo Marciacq, comptroller general of the Republic; Paraguay, Harmodio Gonzalez, manager, Bank of the Republic; Peru, Manuel Gallagher; Uruguay, Roberto E. MacEachen, Minister of Uruguay to Cuba; Venezuela, Diogenes Escalante, Ambasador of Venezuela here.

Ten of the Central American and Caribbean countries have declared war on the Axis, and all other Latin American republics have broken diplomatic relations with the Axis except Argentina and Chile.

The United States delegate will be Edward H. Foley, general counsel of the Treasury Department. He will be assisted by advisers from both the Treasury and State Departments and by L. Werner Knoke, vice president of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.

records.summary_en: The *Washington Daily News* published a chronology of Representative Hamilton Fish's connections to General Rafael Trujillo, including a 1939 goodwill tour of the Dominican Republic. At a New York banquet that year, Fish praised Trujillo as a builder greater than Spanish conquistadores, even as protesters outside condemned the Dominican generalissimo. The paper noted that $25,000 was deposited to Fish's account as part of a $300,000 credit established for Trujillo through the Dominican Legation before Fish sailed for Europe.

El rotativo hizo notar que se giraron 25.000 dólares a la cuenta corriente de Fish mediante una partida de 300.000 dólares habilitada para Trujillo por conducto de la Legación dominicana antes de su viaje a Europa.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported on statements by Dominican Minister Dr. Jesús María Troncoso, who expressed confidence that anti-submarine measures would soon reopen sea lanes for Dominican sugar shipments to Britain while expanding food exports to Puerto Rico. Troncoso asserted that Dominican economic warfare was its main Allied war contribution, defended strong Dominican leaders by comparing them to President Andrew Jackson, and denied that the country was run by a dictatorship. He also praised the agricultural settlement for European refugees established following the 1938 Évian Conference.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* reseñó declaraciones del ministro dominicano Dr. Jesús María Troncoso, quien exteriorizó su convicción de que las operaciones antisubmarinas restablecerían pronto las rutas marítimas para despachar azúcar dominicano hacia Gran Bretaña, incrementando a la par el aprovisionamiento de comestibles para Puerto Rico. Troncoso afirmó que la cooperación económica de su país constituía el aporte bélico medular a la causa aliada, justificó la firmeza de los caudillos patrios equiparándolos con el presidente Andrew Jackson y negó taxativamente que rigiera una dictadura en su patria. Ponderó de igual modo la colonia agrícola de refugiados europeos radicada en el país a consecuencia de la Conferencia de Évian de 1938.
records.passage: States and the Dominican Republic. He is optimistic in regard to the sugar problem, although shipping of the Republic's sugar has been interfered with seriously. He is sure that by the end of next year the Nazi U-boats will have been sufficiently checked to allow for the shipment of the mounting sugar supply to its British markets. Many other exports are sent to the United States. Senor Troncoso's government is developing the exportation of food to nearby Puerto Rico, which is facing an acute food shortage. Though the Republic has an army and navy, the economic warfare they wage is their most effective contribution toward an Allied victory. Unlike her friendly sister republic, Haiti, which is basically French, the tongue and customs of the Dominican Republic are from Spain. The government is modeled after that of the United States and the people enjoy freedom of press and speech. Dr. Troncoso explains that the leaders of the republic often have been strong men who bore out the strength of their convictions with action, but who, nevertheless, were far from being dictators. He compares these leaders to the American President Andrew Jackson, whose opinions in his time brought down cries of dictator. Dr. Troncoso praises the success of the refugee settlement in his country, an idea originated by the republic at the Evian Conference in France in 1939. The agricultural settlement was tested on a scientific basis, with a group of refugees from Europe selected for youth and health and character.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Captain Maurice Marshall Berck, an Army surgeon attached to Walter Reed Hospital, died from severe burns sustained in an apartment fire at the Brighton Hotel. Berck, a prominent New York chest surgeon who married Flor de Oro Trujillo in March 1942, had just returned to Washington from visiting his wife in New York. Firefighters found him unconscious on the floor of the ablaze room, and the cause of the fire remained undetermined.

records.summary_en: The *Wilmington Morning Star* described the geography and population of the Dominican Republic, noting its varied climate ranging from jungles and 10,000-foot peaks to Lake Enriquillo, located 150 feet below sea level. The article reported that the nation's population of roughly 1.75 million was primarily concentrated in northern valleys and around the southern capital of Trujillo City.

La publicación indicó que el millón setecientos cincuenta mil habitantes con que contaba el país se concentraba principalmente en los fértiles valles del Cibao y en el entorno meridional de Ciudad Trujillo.

Haiti also exports an unusual variety of commercial crops. Of these, coffee is well in the lead, followed, normally, by bananas, sisal, cotton, sugar, and cacao. Although the war has brought its usual quota of shipping and trade problems. Haitian economy has been stabilized by recent shipments of coffee and sugar; by cotton crop agreements with the United States, and other financial and trade assistance from the big continental neighbor. Particularly welcome have been orders from the U. S. War Department for Haitian coffee. Haitian sisal, too. is proving a valuable fiber to take the place of some of this lost raw material of the Orient, while rubber planting there also is expected to help meet war needs. A significant indication of increased interest in the United States is seen in a recent decree making English a required subject in Haitian schools. In an area about half the size of Virginia, the Dominican Republic presents samples of some of the world's most varied climate and scenery—from humid jungle to cactus-dotted desert, from ten thousand-foot mountain heights to the Lake de Enriquillo, 150 feet below sea level and saltier than sea water. Most of the Dominicans, who number roughly a million and three-quarters, are concentrated either in the lowlands and valleys of the north, or around the capital, Trujillo City, in the south. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that President Roosevelt submitted nominations elevating several U.S. ministers in Central America and the Caribbean to ambassadorial rank. March 30 (Delayed).—Ivan "Cy" Peterman, correspondent of the Philadelphia Inquirer, became the second American newspaper casualty in the Tunisian campaign today when he broke a wrist diving into a ditch east of El Guetar to escape strafing by a German plane. Mr. Peterman, a former sports columnist, also suffered head cuts when he struck a stone, but his helmet protected him from serious injury. With him in a jeep at the time of the accident were Phil Ault of United Press and Michael Chinigo of International News Service. records.summary_en: The *Washington Daily News* reported on the diplomatic elevation of missions between the United States and seven Caribbean and Central American nations, including the Dominican Republic and Haiti, from legations to full embassies. Under reciprocal agreements, the respective ministers were elevated to ambassadors, leaving Canada as the only Western Hemisphere mission remaining at ministerial rank. Latin American diplomats gathered in Washington to celebrate the confirmations and exchange congratulations.
records.summary_es: *The Washington Daily News* reseñó el acto solemne de jerarquización institucional por el cual las misiones mutuas entre Estados Unidos y siete repúblicas centroamericanas y antillanas —entre ellas la República Dominicana y Haití— fueron elevadas de legaciones a embajadas de primera clase. Conforme a convenios de reciprocidad, los respectivos ministros pasaron a ser embajadores extraordinarios, quedando Canadá como la única sede diplomática continental que conservaba rango de legación. Los dignatarios hispanoamericanos se congregaron en Washington para festejar las acreditaciones e intercambiar salutaciones de estilo.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Flor de Oro Trujillo, daughter of Dominican President Rafael Trujillo, arrived en route to Washington to assume duties as first secretary of the Dominican Embassy. Miss Trujillo, whose husband Captain Maurice Berck died in an accident four months prior, expressed her desire to study international law, pursue diplomacy, and observe American women's customs to introduce them to her home country. She noted that she was fluent in Portuguese, German, French, and English in addition to Spanish.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó del arribo a Washington de la señorita Flor de Oro Trujillo, hija del presidente dominicano Rafael Trujillo, a fin de incorporarse a la embajada de su patria en calidad de primera secretaria. La señorita Trujillo, cuyo cónyuge, el capitán Maurice Berck, pereciera en un infortunio cuatro meses antes, exteriorizó su inclinación hacia el estudio del derecho internacional, el ejercicio diplomático y el conocimiento de las costumbres cívicas de la mujer estadounidense para aplicarlas en su tierra natal. Añadió que dominaba a la perfección el portugués, alemán, francés e inglés, además de su castellano natal.

Miss Trujillo, daughter of the President of the Dominican Republic, arrived yesterday en route to Washington, where she will assume her post as first secretary to the Dominican Embassy. "This is a big chance my father has given me." the attractive brunette declared, "and I am going to study hard so that I will not disappoint him." The young diplomat has spent the last two years, until the past month, in the United States, as the wife of Capt. Maurice Berck. Capt. Berck. she said, was killed in an accident In Washington four months ago. Miss Trujillo, who was educated abroad, said she plans to pursue a diplomatic career and will study international law. She already speaks four languages in addition to Spanish—Portuguese, German, French and English. She was to leave today by plane for New York, where she will spend a week before assuming her post. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Don Anselmo Copello, Dominican Ambassador to the United States, died at age 65 in Doctors Hospital following pneumonia and a heart attack. records.full_text:
Don Anselmo Copello
Funeral Arranged
For Tomorrow

Members of the diplomatic corps and high Government officials will attend funeral services for Don Anselmo Copello, Ambassador from the Dominican Republic, at 11 a.m tomorrow at the Sacred Heart Church, Sixteenth street and Park road N.W. After temporary burial in Arlington Cemetery, the body will be taken to the Dominican Republic.

The Ambassador, who was 65, died yesterday in Doctors Hospital of a heart attack which followed pneumonia. He had been ill two days.

His work was praised in the following statement made yesterday by Secretary of State Stettinius:

“I have been greatly grieved to learn of the death of the distinguished Ambassador of the Dominican Republic. His excellency Anselmo Copella. In my association with him in dealing with the problems of mutual interest, I have come to know his outstanding qualities as a diplomat and as a friend.

“He has represented his country with distinction and has always evinced a most helpful spirit of cooperation in dealing with matters of common concern. The Dominican people will rightly mourn the passing of a gifted statesman and his many friends in this country will sincerely share their sorrow.”

Senor Copello returned to Washington Monday from the Dominican Republic, where he had been on official business for three months. He was accompanied by his only son, Jeronimo.

Before his appointment as Ambassador to this country in November, 1943, Senor Copello had never served as a government official except for several honorary posts. His credentials were received by President Roosevelt on December 20, 1943. He succeeded Dr. J. M. Troncoso, now Secretary of the Treasury of the Dominican Republic.

President of the principal tobacco company of the Dominican Republic, Senor Copello’s home was in Santiago.

Besides his widow, Senora de Copello, and his son, he is survived by four daughters, Adelina, Argentina, Ileana and Margarita. The family lives at the Embassy, 4530 Sixteenth street N.W.

Dr. J. R. Rodriguez, Minister Counselor, will direct the affairs of the Embassy until further arrangements are made by his government.

Cooperative health programs to control malaria were launched in eighteen nations, including the Dominican Republic and Haiti, to sustain the production of vital war materials. The article emphasized that these initiatives, along with agricultural and technical assistance, were mutually beneficial cooperative efforts rather than unilateral handouts.

El informe recalcó que estos planes, junto al respaldo técnico y agrícola, obedecían a esquemas bilaterales equitativos de beneficio común y no a dádivas discrecionales unilaterales.

records.headline: Americas Plan Slap at Franco
records.summary_en: Consultations are under way among the foreign offices of the American nations over a simultaneous diplomatic break with the government of Generalissimo Francisco Franco in Spain, after the Uruguayan Senate forwarded a recommendation for a break and both houses of the Peruvian Congress approved one. In Central America and the Caribbean, Guatemala, Honduras, Panama, the Dominican Republic and Haiti have already broken relations with Franco, and Mexico never recognized his dictatorship. A State Department spokesman in Washington denied a report that the United States and other American nations had agreed on a collective break, but other sources predicted that further diplomatic breaks with Spain could be expected.

En Centroamérica y el Caribe, Guatemala, Honduras, Panamá, la República Dominicana y Haití ya han roto relaciones con Franco, y México nunca reconoció su dictadura. Un portavoz del Departamento de Estado en Washington negó que los Estados Unidos y otras naciones americanas hubieran acordado una ruptura colectiva, pero otras fuentes previeron que podrían esperarse nuevas rupturas diplomáticas con España.

records.headline: Venezuelan Cabinet Post Goes to Ex-GI
records.summary_en: Luis Valmore Rodríguez, a 45-year-old former United States Army sergeant and editor of El País, will be sworn in as interior minister in Venezuela's new revolutionary government, which seized power in a four-day uprising that overthrew President Isaías Medina Angarita. Named to the post by his friend, revolutionary president Rómulo Betancourt, he will oversee the government's relations with American oil companies and other foreign investors, and has assured them he will respect their rights. Interim foreign minister Carlos Morales said the junta would meet all international obligations undertaken by the previous government and was seeking foreign recognition; asked about future relations with Franco's Spain, Trujillo's Dominican Republic and the Argentine regime, he made no commitment but said his people were not in favor of such regimes.

Morgan, who performed numerous charitable operations for the underprivileged in the Dominican Republic without accepting payment. Dr. Morgan commended the Dominican government for its cooperation and health advancements, noting the presence of government hospitals in Trujillo City and Santiago prior to the construction of Morgan Hospital. records.summary_en: The Midland Journal reported on upcoming celebrations marking the 450th anniversary of the founding of Santo Domingo, featuring a historic pageant and an address by President Rafael Trujillo. The article noted that the capital was rebuilt along modern lines following a devastating hurricane in 1930 and subsequently renamed Ciudad Trujillo by its citizens despite Trujillo's objections. It also praised the republic's fertile agriculture and highlighted its strong standing in Washington following its early war declarations against Japan and Germany in December 1941.

El artículo consignó que la capital había renacido bajo directrices modernas luego del desolador huracán de 1930, siendo rebautizada como Ciudad Trujillo por voluntad popular no obstante la renuencia inicial de Trujillo. Destacó asimismo la fecunda fertilidad agrícola nacional y el sólido predicamento de que gozaba el régimen en Washington tras su pronta declaración de guerra a Japón y Alemania en diciembre de 1941.

records.summary_en: The Springfield Weekly Republican reported on the extensive modernization of the Dominican Republic under President Rafael Trujillo over a sixteen-year span achieved without foreign loans. Improvements included a twenty percent decrease in illiteracy, hundreds of newly built schools, seventy new bridges, and irrigation projects reclaiming 85,000 acres. The article noted that the rebuilt capital, renamed Ciudad Trujillo by citizens, was growing into a major Caribbean tourist destination.

Los adelantos abarcaban una reducción del veinte por ciento en el analfabetismo, centenares de escuelas recién levantadas, setenta puentes nuevos e infraestructuras de regadío que recuperaron 85.000 acres de tierra. El informe agregaba que la reconstruida capital, rebautizada Ciudad Trujillo por la población, se afianzaba como un emporio turístico caribeño de primer orden.

Illiteracy dropped 20 per cent due to the building of hundreds of new schools and the allotment of 13 per cent of the national budget to furthering education. Beautifully paved roads and 70 new bridges put formerly isolated regions into easy communication with one another and with the capital. Vast irrigation projects brought 85,000 acres of land under cultivation. Factories employ twice as many people and produce three times as many exportable items as previously. New hospitals. clothing manufacture, water works, schools and public buildings transformed an ancient city of ruins into a modern metropolis. records.headline: Eye witness reports received today frem Matanzas on the North Coast
records.summary_en: Eyewitness reports from Matanzas, on the north coast, said a tidal wave from Sunday's earthquake swept as much as a mile inland, catching even a party fleeing by automobile, and left only eight of the town's 300 houses standing. Residents had taken refuge in trees and high places, and reports from Matanzas and Nagua said frightened inhabitants in the forests were suffering from hunger, with authorities considering dropping food from airplanes, as wrecked communications made the damage across more than 11 towns hard to assess.
records.summary_es: Testimonios desde Matanzas, en la costa norte, decían que un maremoto provocado por el terremoto del domingo penetró hasta una milla tierra adentro, alcanzó incluso a un grupo que huía en automóvil y dejó en pie solo ocho de las 300 casas del pueblo. Los vecinos se habían refugiado en árboles y lugares altos, y los informes de Matanzas y Nagua decían que habitantes asustados en los bosques padecían hambre, mientras las autoridades consideraban lanzar alimentos desde aviones y las comunicaciones destruidas dificultaban evaluar los daños en más de 11 pueblos.
records.passage: range, stricken Sunday by an earthquake and tidal wave which took a toll of at least two dead and damaged more than 11 towns in this Carribean Republic. The eyewitness said the residents had been forewarned and had taken refuge in trees and high places. Only eight of the 300 houses in Matanzas were reported left standing. Wrecked telegraph and communication facilities made it difficult to get a clear picture of the damage wrought by the quake which apparently centered in the deepest point in the Atlantic ocean, approximately 50 miles off the east coast of the Dominican Republic. Reports from the Matanzas and Nagua regions said that frightened inhabitants had taken refuge in the forests and were suffering from hunger. Authorities were considering dropping food from airplanes. A search started, and airports along both Florida coasts were checked without success, as were other Gulf areas. Meanwhile no Washington agency could be found that would admit ordering the alert.

Then, yesterday afternoon, the State Department acknowledged it had heard the rumor and said it had relayed it to the Customs Bureau and other agencies for investigation.

The statement disclosed that the State Department has had in effect for months a general alert, based on “general rumors of revolutionary plotting,” to make sure that “United States territory would not be used for conspiracy.”

Rumor Involves 7 Planes.

The statement, issued by Press Officer Reginald Mitchell, said the State Department has been receiving “rumors” and “fragmentary reports” of impending trouble in the Caribbean area but has declined to comment because of their unsubstantial nature. The statement continued:

“One such rumor was to the effect that there were seven combat planes at an airfield in Florida ready to depart for a Caribbean destination. The department Friday immediately communicated this rumor to the Customs Bureau and other United States Government agencies concerned and requested that an investigation be made and that these alleged planes be prevented from leaving the United States.

“The department has been informed that the Customs Bureau promptly notified its Florida headquarters office at Tampa which in turn alerted its subordinate customs offices at Miami, Jacksonville, West Palm Beach and elsewhere in Florida. The department has received no further information in this particular matter.

“The department heard general rumors of revolutionary plotting in the Caribbean area as long ago as January of this year and in an effort to make sure that United States territory would not be used for conspiracy alerted the appropriate law enforcement agencies, which since that date have kept a scrupulous watch.”

Easy Flight for Fighters.

At least some of the rumors were based on reports in Haitian and Dominican newspapers.

The P38 Lightning and the P51 Mustang, Army fighter planes extensively used in the war, would easily be able to fly from Florida to the Dominican Republic. The shortest airline distance is a little over 650 miles. There are the Bahama Islands and the tip of Cuba in between.

A War Department official said some Lightnings and Mustangs have been sold as surplus and may be in the hands of civilians.

records.summary_en: A historical account traces the United States customs receivership to the Dominican resolution of March 31, 1905, known as the Modus Vivendi, which conceded to the United States the same rights over customs income as an earlier pact. records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that federal customs authorities in Baltimore detained the *Patria*, a converted infantry landing craft suspected of involvement in anti-Trujillo activities. An investigation revealed the vessel was manned largely by affluent Dominican exiles and had been acquired by Cuban Cruz Alonso, though a search found no weapons or ammunition. The State Department stated the action enforced strict policy prohibiting the use of United States territory to launch civil strife in foreign nations.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que la policía aduanera federal destacada en Baltimore aprehendió al *Patria*, un buque de desembarco de infantería modificado sospechoso de involucramiento en actividades conspirativas contra Trujillo. Las pesquisas comprobaron que la dotación estaba formada mayoritariamente por acaudalados desterrados dominicanos y que la nave había sido adquirida por el cubano Cruz Alonso, si bien el registro ocular no arrojó hallazgo de municiones ni fusiles. El Departamento de Estado aclaró que la retención obedecía a la estricta política neutral de proscribir la utilización del suelo estadounidense para fraguar expediciones bélicas contra Estados soberanos.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Cuban political leaders sharply condemned President Ramon Grau San Martin following the Cuban army's suppression of a 1,500-man expedition organized to invade the Dominican Republic. Senators Eduardo Chibas and Aurelio Alvarez accused Grau of using the anti-Trujillo movement to destabilize Cuban politics and consolidate personal dictatorial power. Military authorities detained over 1,100 expedition members and seized four ships along with extensive stockpiles of arms and explosives.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que destacados dirigentes políticos de Cuba enjuiciaron con dureza al presidente Ramón Grau San Martín tras la desarticulación por el ejército cubano de una expedición de 1.500 combatientes aprestada para invadir la República Dominicana. Los senadores Eduardo Chibás y Aurelio Álvarez acusaron a Grau de instrumentalizar la conspiración antitrujillista para subvertir el orden interno de Cuba y afianzar prerrogativas dictatoriales propias. Las fuerzas castrenses arrestaron a más de 1.100 conjurados e incautaron cuatro embarcaciones mercantes y nutridos arsenales de pertrechos, proyectiles y dinamita.

The Senator previously had been considered one of the President's staunchest defenders. Senator Aurelio Alvarez, leader of the opposition, accused President Grau of having "armed gangs which sought to invade the Dominican Republic, in order to create an atmosphere of violence in Cuba and thus perpetuate himself in power." records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Cuban magistrate Evelio Tabio ordered the release of nearly 1,200 participants in the aborted anti-Trujillo invasion expedition, holding only its purported leaders in custody. A captured diary published by the newspaper *Hoy* detailed training at Holguin and miserable conditions on Cayo Confites, where troops endured internal infighting, accidental drownings, and failed logistics aboard vessels including the *Aurora*, *Berta*, and *Angelita*. The collapse of the operation culminated in mass surrenders at Guinchos Cay and Antilla.

Un diario de bitácora ocupado y divulgado por el diario *Hoy* detalló los adiestramientos castrenses en Holguín y las precarias penalidades sufridas en Cayo Confites, donde los reclutas padecieron motines internos, ahogamientos accidentales y severos descalabros de abasto a bordo de los barcos *Aurora*, *Berta* y *Angelita*. El fracaso del complot culminó con rendiciones multitudinarias en Cayo Guinchos y la bahía de Antilla.

records.summary_en: Twenty-six alleged chiefs of a 1,007-man expeditionary force to depose President Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic were freed in Havana under bonds of $5,000 each. Special Magistrate Evelio Tabio charged them with jeopardizing the peace of the state and taking enlistments without authorization of the Cuban government. The group, mostly Dominicans and Cubans, included eight generals; the rest of the force, including three men from the United States, had been freed after surrendering on Guinchos Cay and at Antilla.

El magistrado especial Evelio Tabio los acusó de poner en peligro la paz del Estado y de realizar alistamientos sin autorización del gobierno cubano. El grupo, en su mayoría dominicanos y cubanos, incluía ocho generales; el resto de la fuerza, incluidos tres hombres de Estados Unidos, había sido liberado tras rendirse en Cayo Guinchos y en Antilla.

Special Magistrate Evelio Tabio of the Supreme Tribunal accepted the bonds from a security company, which refused to say for whom it was acting Judge Tabio had ordered the 26 men charged with “having jeopardized the peace of the state” and having taken enlistments “without legal authorization of the Cuban government.” The group, mostly Dominicans and Cubans, included eight generals. Waddel, 27, and Thomas Sawyer, 26, both of New York city. The force surrendered to Cuban authorities early last week on Guinchos Cay off the North Cuban coast and at the port of Antilla.

Cuban Blames Trujillo For Arms Plot Charges By the Associated Press JACKSONVILLE, Fla., Dec. 9.— Manolo Castro, director of the Cuban Sports Commission, charged yesterday that enmity of Rafael Trujillo was responsible for his implication in an alleged plot to export arms to Cuba for use in an unsuccessful revolt against the Dominican Republic President last summer. Castro, who came to Jacksonville for arraignment on an indictment charging illegal exportation of arms and high explosives from the United States, pleaded not guilty before Federal Judge Louie W. Strum. The case was set for trial January 5. Not guilty pleas also were entered by Chester L. Miller and Percy H. Cyr, both airplane pilots of Hasbrouck Heights, N. J. Hollis B. Smith, Palisades Park, N. J.. who is alleged to have purchased the arms, pleaded guilty. Smith was permitted to remain under bond pending disposition of the charges against the other defendants. records.headline: DIPLOMATIC NOTES FOR DREW PEARSON A plot by the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: A White Paper circulated by the Venezuelan Embassy charged that the Dominican Republic was plotting to send an armed invasion against Venezuela, accusing dictator Trujillo of harboring Venezuelan enemies and purchasing arms for them in Brazil. As proof it attached a photostat of an intercepted letter from Trujillo's private secretary to Dominican foreign offices around the world, instructing them to attend to exiled Venezuelans, enemies of Caracas, and to tell them they would find in the Dominican Republic refuge, hospitality and protection, personal as well as political. The White Paper added that the Venezuelan government had concrete proof the Dominican Republic had long sponsored an armed movement against Venezuela.
records.summary_es: Un Libro Blanco distribuido por la Embajada de Venezuela acusó a la República Dominicana de tramar el envío de una invasión armada contra Venezuela, señalando al dictador Trujillo de albergar a enemigos venezolanos y comprar armas para ellos en Brasil. Como prueba adjuntaba una fotocopia de una carta interceptada del secretario privado de Trujillo a las oficinas dominicanas en el exterior, con instrucciones de atender a los venezolanos exiliados, enemigos de Caracas, y decirles que en la República Dominicana encontrarían refugio, hospitalidad y protección, tanto personal como política. El Libro Blanco añadía que el gobierno venezolano tenía pruebas concretas de que la República Dominicana auspiciaba desde hacía tiempo un movimiento armado contra Venezuela.

Page A-4 President Truman notified Congress today that he intends to ask more money, for military aid, for Greece and Turkey. He gave no indication of how much new assistance will be needed, however, in transmitting to Congress a report on use of the $400,000,000 voted last year to help Greece and Turkey resist Communism. records.summary_en: The Atlanta Daily World reported that Brooklyn Dodgers first baseman Jackie Robinson reported to spring training in Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic, where he was greeted enthusiastically as a baseball hero. Local spectators and schoolchildren cheered his appearance in the dugout, batting practice, and drills at first base. records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the Costa Rican government appealed to Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic for military assistance against insurgent forces led by Jose Figueres. Rebel troops sabotaged electrical installations at Brazil and launched surprise assaults at Quepos, threatening the advance toward Cartago. The armed conflict arose following the disputed presidential election of Otilio Ulate, which the government-controlled Congress had annulled in favor of Rafael Calderon Guardia.

Los destacamentos insurrectos sabotearon redes de energía en la localidad de Brasil y acometieron asaltos sorpresivos en Quepos, poniendo en jaque el avance hacia Cartago. La contienda intestina estalló a raíz de los controvertidos sufragios presidenciales que ungieron a Otilio Ulate, los cuales fueron anulados por el Congreso oficialista para beneficiar al candidato Rafael Calderón Guardia.

Costa Rica Asks Aid From Two Republics By the Associated Press SAN JOSE, Costa Rica, Mar. 27.— The Costa Rican government has renewed appeals to Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic for help in fighting the Figueres revolutionary forces, reliable sources said tonight, What the response would be no one could say. Nicaraguan troops have been fighting on the government's side and some are still here, although an order for their return home has been issued. Rebel troops, led by Jose Figueres, slipped through government lines this morning and dynamited power plant installations at Brazil on the Pacific Coast. They also began a surprise attack against government troops at Quepos north of Dominical which the government has been trying to hold since last week. To the south Figueres soldiers moved down the side of Cerro de la Muerte Mountain toward Cartago and apparently were ready to storm that ancient capital of Costa Rica. The fighting which began 17 days ago is the outgrowth of last month's turbulent and disputed presidential election in which Otilio Ulate was elected. records.summary_en: The Evening Star analyzed strategic vulnerabilities in Caribbean defenses, warning of potential submarine threats to the Panama Canal and regional bases. The analysis noted ongoing armed conflict in Costa Rica, where government forces reportedly received backing from Dominicans, Nicaraguans, and Hondurans against rebels supporting Otilio Ulate. The author cautioned that a communist victory would leave American defense lines bordered by hostile regimes, with the unsympathetic Dominican government positioned centrally in the region.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* examinó las vulnerabilidades operativas en el dispositivo de seguridad caribeño, previniendo acerca de posibles amenazas submarinas contra el canal de Panamá y las bases tácticas comarcanas. records.full_text:
Dominican Republic
Asks New Airing of
Dispute With Cuba

By the Associated Press

A long-standing feud between Cuba and the Dominican Republic was spotlighted yesterday when the Dominican government formally asked for another airing of troubles between the two countries.

The development occurred in an exchange of notes between the Dominican government and the five-nation Inter-American Peace Committee.

The latter group was set up by the 21 hemisphere foreign ministers in 1940 to seek peaceful settlement of Inter-American disputes. The United States, Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Cuba are members.

After three weeks of discussion the committee Thursday night sent a note to the Dominican government expressing concern over special war powers granted to President Rafael Trujillo. The Dominican Republic replied that they resulted from a “profound state of emergency” in the Caribbean.

War Powers Granted.

Trujillo got from the Dominican Congress this month power to declare war on any country which he considers is harboring plotters working against him.

The move was directed to Cuba where Mr. Trupillo charged a new attempt to mount an invasion of the Dominican Republic is going on. This was strongly denied by Cuba.

The committee’s note asked Mr. Trujillo not to use force unless under armed attack in accordance with terms of the Rio mutual defense treaty.

In reply, Dominican Secretary of State Virgilio Diaz Ordonez said “no other country or government would fail to act in the same way as we are doing now.” But he added that the republic would respond to any conciliatory gesture to end the “abnormality with which we are confronted.”

His note added the government is ready to receive recommendations from the committee.

The feud between the two Caribbean nations is an old story to the committee. In 1948, the group got the two nations to agree to settle their differences through diplomatic channels. The Dominican charge then was based on an unsuccessful attempt in 1947 by various groups of exiles to create an invasion force in Cuba to overthrow Mr. Trujillo.

The following year the Dominicans went before the committee with the assertion the same group was being outfitted anew in Cuba.

A few months ago the committee issued a 14-point statement designed to calm Caribbean tension after an airborne invasion of the Dominican Republic failed.

In the meantime, it settled a flareup between the neighboring Dominican Republic and Haiti when the latter charged Mr. Trujillo was personally involved in a plot to ove-thorw the Port-au-Prince government.

Trujillo had initially demanded the authority after accusing Cuba, Haiti, and Guatemala of sheltering anti-regime conspirators. He stated the repeal was intended to ease regional tensions and foster diplomatic solutions to Caribbean conflicts.

Trujillo había exigido inicialmente dicha autoridad tras acusar a Cuba, Haití y Guatemala de cobijar a conspiradores contrarios a su régimen. Declaró que la revocación tenía como propósito aliviar las tensiones regionales y propiciar soluciones diplomáticas a los conflictos caribeños.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the OAS investigating committee issued recommendations to preserve peace in the Caribbean under threat of Rio Treaty sanctions. The committee urged the Dominican government to halt official support for seditious movements against neighboring states and adhere strictly to its 1949 pact with Haiti. Additionally, Cuba and Guatemala were instructed to dismantle armed exile expeditions on their soil and halt illicit arms trafficking by the Caribbean Legion.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star published an editorial evaluating the OAS committee report on Caribbean political turmoil involving Haiti, the Dominican Republic, Cuba, and Guatemala. The committee exonerated Haiti while censuring the Dominican Republic, Cuba, and Guatemala for treaty violations and support of subversive exile plots. The editorial endorsed the proposed creation of a watchdog committee backed by Rio Treaty sanctions to maintain regional stability.

El editorial respaldó la propuesta de creación de una comisión de vigilancia amparada en sanciones del Tratado de Río para mantener la estabilidad regional.

records.summary_en: The Ohio Daily-Express published a personal account of a cruise in the Gulf of Gonave with Haitian President Dumarsais Estime, during which American naval vessels offered a presidential salute. President Estime expressed a desire to attract African American entrepreneurs and capital to build domestic enterprises like sugar refineries, canning plants, and cement factories. The article highlighted the success of Capt. J. O. Plinton, a former Tuskegee-trained fighter pilot who founded a thriving modern dry cleaning business in Port-au-Prince.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the OAS investigating committee led by Dr. Jose A. Mora issued unprecedented findings condemning state-sponsored subversion in the Caribbean. The report found President Rafael Trujillo's regime guilty of aiding plots to overthrow the Haitian government, while finding Cuban and Guatemalan officials complicit in Caribbean Legion expeditions against Trujillo. The committee urged the OAS Council to actively enforce its authority by invoking Rio Treaty sanctions against future violators.

El informe declaró culpable al régimen del presidente Rafael Trujillo de colaborar en planes para derrocar al gobierno haitiano, al tiempo que determinó la complicidad de funcionarios cubanos y guatemaltecos en expediciones de la Legión del Caribe contra Trujillo. La comisión instó al Consejo de la OEA a ejercer enérgicamente su autoridad invocando las sanciones del Tratado de Río contra futuros infractores.

It also established that officials and prominent citizens of Cuba and Guatemala had abetted "the Caribbean Legion” and other sub versive groups in repeated plans to invade the Dominican Republic and unseat Dictator Trujillo. Stronger Council Urged The stinging report of the fact finders is not only an innovation, but unprecedented in hemisphere relations. But the Mora commit tee feels that it is not enough merely to turn the spotlight of publicity upon the would-be ag gressors. Exposing the culprits will not be enough to put an end to political bickering and back biting in the American neigh borhood. The committee has called upon the Council to take steps to make itself more positive, not to say more powerful, in enforcing its decisions against such trouble makers. records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that federal authorities arrested members of a counterfeit ring accused of attempting to pass $3 million in fake U.S. currency into the Cuban national treasury. In court proceedings before U.S. Commissioner Edward W. McDonald, it was alleged that the proceeds were intended to finance a revolution against the Dominican Republic. While the federal grand jury indictment focused on the counterfeit scheme and named two Cubans, it did not explicitly cite the Dominican invasion plot.

En las actuaciones judiciales ante el comisionado estadounidense Edward W. McDonald, se alegó que las ganancias estaban destinadas a financiar una revolución contra la República Dominicana. By the Associated Press. SINGAPORE — Burning taxicabs — a practice that has been stopped for almost two months — is back on the Singapore scene. Arsonists got busy the other night in the regular manner. Two Chinese youths engaged the taxicab, ordered the Malaya driver to go into a less guarded area and there kicked out the driver. They then fired the cab with the help of two waiting fellow arsonists. U. S. Doctor Removes Appendix of Shah of Iran. By the Associated Press. TEHERAN, Iran, July 5. — An American doctor removed the appendix of Shah Mohammed Reza Pahlevi today and the 32-year-old ruler was reported resting comfortably. A court official described the operation as "a simple appendectomy with no complications." A later bulletin from the court ministry disclosed that the doctors also removed a scar from the Shah's left shoulder. This was left by the attempt on the Shah's life in 1949. Four American and three Iranian doctors were present at the operating room in Teheran's Bank Melli Hospital. The actual operation was performed by Dr. Frank Glenn, chief surgeon at New York Hospital.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that prominent hotels in the Dominican Republic were expanding recreational amenities to attract American tourists. Features highlighted included swimming pools, tennis courts, open-air dancing, nightly entertainment, and a gambling casino. The edition also covered congressional approval of emergency housing funds to assist victims of Midwest flooding.

The Senate gave the final nod to the emergency aid plan, pre viously approved by the House. It would authorize use of part of a $25 million emergency flood re lief fund voted by Congress to supply trailers and other tempo rary shelters. The measure, which now goes to the White House for approval, also would permit the Federal Housing Administration to insure low-cost homes—built to replace flood-destroyed houses—up to 100 per cent of their value. Present law limits such insurance to 95 per cent of value. records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported on deliberations at the Japanese peace treaty conference in San Francisco. Representatives from Mexico, the Dominican Republic, Chile, and Bolivia endorsed the proposed treaty and pledged their signatures, with Soviet delegate Andrei Gromyko standing alone in opposition. The Soviet Union introduced sweeping amendments demanding the withdrawal of U.S. forces, demilitarization, and great-power veto rights.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó sobre las deliberaciones en la conferencia del tratado de paz con Japón celebrada en San Francisco. Representantes de México, la República Dominicana, Chile y Bolivia respaldaron el proyecto de tratado y comprometieron sus firmas, quedando el delegado soviético Andréi Gromyko como el único opositor. La Unión Soviética presentó enmiendas de gran alcance en las que exigía la retirada de las fuerzas de EE. UU., la desmilitarización y derechos de veto para las grandes potencias.
records.passage: said it opened a new era in the history of Japan and bolstered prospects for peace in the Pacific. In a session opening at 10 a.m. (1 p.m., EDT) today speeches were scheduled by the delegates of El Salvador, Norway, Haiti, Nicaragua, Egypt, Laos and Ceylon. This was to be followed by an aft ernoon session (6 p.m., EDT), in which representatives of Pakistan, France and the Philippines were to speak. French Foreign Minister Schuman will make the address; for his country. Russia Seeks Veto. Mr. Gromyko’s amendments would (1) compel the withdrawal of all American troops from Japan 90 days after the treaty went into force, (2) prevent any mili tary alliance by Japan “against any power” which fought against Japan in World War II, and (3) require demilitarization of certain Japanese coastal areas. Russia also would get a veto over the treaty along with other great powers. The Soviet amendments further would (1) take the Ryukyu and Bonin Islands from United States administration and give them to Japan, (2) legally secure Russia’s 1 own hold on the Kurile Islands and South Sakhalin and (3) pro vide for reparations from Japan to nations which Japanese forces occupied in the war. records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Dominican Ambassador Luis Francisco Thomen conferred the Order of Juan Pablo Duarte upon Dr. Murdock for his contributions to public health in the Dominican Republic. The ceremony and embassy reception coincided with sessions of the Pan American Sanitary Bureau and the World Health Organization. Guests including State Department officials and medical leaders were served traditional Dominican specialties alongside American delicacies.

La ceremonia y recepción en la embajada coincidieron con las sesiones de la Oficina Sanitaria Panamericana y la Organización Mundial de la Salud. A los invitados, entre quienes figuraban funcionarios del Departamento de Estado y dirigentes médicos, se les sirvieron especialidades tradicionales dominicanas junto a manjares estadounidenses.

records.summary_en: The Atlanta Daily World reported that President Rafael Trujillo resumed direct control of the Dominican government after temporarily delegating executive authority to his brother, General Hector Bienvenido Trujillo, since February. The dispatch observed that Trujillo frequently rotated titular authority between himself and his brother without public explanation. It noted that the ruling Dominican Party had nominated Hector for the presidency in upcoming May elections, despite executive decisions remaining concentrated in Rafael's hands.
records.summary_es: El *Atlanta Daily World* informó que el presidente Rafael Trujillo reasumió el control directo del gobierno dominicano tras haber delegado temporalmente el poder ejecutivo en su hermano, el general Héctor Bienvenido Trujillo, desde febrero. El despacho observaba que Trujillo alternaba con frecuencia la titularidad del mando con su hermano sin ofrecer explicaciones públicas. Señaló asimismo que el oficialista Partido Dominicano había postulado a Héctor a la presidencia para las elecciones venideras de mayo, aun cuando las decisiones ejecutivas seguían concentradas en manos de Rafael.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the United States concluded a ten-year bilateral pact with the Dominican Republic authorizing guided missile monitoring stations to close the observation gap between the Bahamas and Puerto Rico. Under the agreement, unarmed test missiles launched from Florida would fly over Dominican coastal waters rather than over the mainland. U.S. military personnel operating the tracking sites were capped at 300 individuals, expandable up to 500 under exceptional circumstances.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que Estados Unidos concertó un pacto bilateral de diez años con la República Dominicana que autorizaba estaciones de rastreo de misiles guiados para cerrar la brecha de observación entre las Bahamas y Puerto Rico. En virtud del acuerdo, los misiles de prueba desarmados lanzados desde Florida sobrevolarían aguas costeras dominicanas en lugar de territorio continental. El personal militar estadounidense que operaría los puestos de seguimiento tenía un límite máximo de 300 efectivos, ampliable hasta 500 en circunstancias excepcionales.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the Dominican Republic and the Republic of Turkey signed a friendship treaty in Washington pledging perpetual peace between the two nations. The agreement was signed at the Turkish Embassy by Dominican Ambassador Luis Francisco Thomen and Turkish Ambassador Feridun C. Erkin. The accord established a framework for future bilateral treaties addressing commerce, navigation, consular rights, intellectual property, and extradition.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que la República Dominicana y la República de Turquía firmaron un tratado de amistad en Washington comprometiéndose a una paz perpetua entre ambas naciones. El acuerdo fue suscrito en la embajada turca por el embajador dominicano Luis Francisco Thomen y el embajador turco Feridun C. Erkin. El pacto estableció las bases para futuros tratados bilaterales sobre comercio, navegación, derechos consulares, propiedad intelectual y extradición.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Cuban Foreign Minister Aureliano Sanchez Arango denounced the Dominican seizure of a vessel and the subsequent 30-year hard-labor sentences imposed on its crew for alleged subversive plotting. Sanchez Arango accused the ship's captain, Brito, of acting as a Dominican spy who delivered the craft and kidnapped its crew under shifting pretenses before being convicted alongside them. Because diplomatic protests proved futile, Cuba appealed the maritime incident to the Inter-American Peace Commission.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores de Cuba, Aureliano Sánchez Arango, denunció la captura de una embarcación por parte de la República Dominicana y las posteriores condenas a 30 años de trabajos forzados impuestas a su tripulación por supuestas actividades subversivas. Sánchez Arango acusó al capitán del barco, Brito, de actuar como espía dominicano que entregó la nave y secuestró a su tripulación bajo pretextos cambiantes antes de ser condenado junto a ellos. Dado que las protestas diplomáticas resultaron infructuosas, Cuba recurrió ante la Comisión Interamericana de Paz por el incidente marítimo.
records.passage: The Minister declared the sei zure was entirely illegal and can not be condoned by the nations of the world. He said the crew members were held incommuni cado for three months and even tually were sentenced to serve 30 years at hard labor on charges of plotting against the security of the Dominican Republic. He said the charges were baseless. Mr. Sanchez Arango declared Capt. Brito told two different stories. At first, the minister re ported, the skipper (wearing a uniform of the Dominican Navy) said he had been on special as signment for his Government, with instruction to deliver his ves sel to the warship. The Minister said the Dominican authorities apparently realized this showed Capt. Brito to be a spy in Cuban territory who kidnaped the crew.' Captain Imprisoned. Brito said he was a revolutionary conspiring against the Trujillo regime, that he realized he was in the wrong and therefore signaled to the warship for inter ception. But he was imprisoned, like the rest of the crew. Negotiations through regular diplomatic channels have availed Cuba nothing, Mr. Sanchez Arango said.
